oaiso run --image IMAGE --environment-lock codex-dock.lock.json -d
oaiso run --start-hook 'npm ci' --readiness 'test -f node_modules/.package-lock.json' --readiness-timeout 2m -d
  • Lifecycle limits require reap --watch or periodic Go API Reap calls.
  • No host service is installed automatically; limits stop being applied while the supervisor is down.
  • Idle means time since management execution activity, not guest CPU/filesystem activity.
  • Updated nodes protect registered jobs and exec/PTY sessions; disable idle limits for main-agent work or activity outside the management API.
  • Explicit maximum lifetime can still stop busy workers.
  • Stop revokes tokens; removal uses existing ownership checks and deletion journals.

  • Zero retention never deletes a worker.

  • Environment locks pin the node OCI image digest and SHA-256 hashes of explicitly selected source files.

  • New lock files are created exclusively.
  • Source or image changes reject launch.
  • Include dependency lockfiles to cover package versions.
  • Start hooks run sequentially inside the guest after auth setup and before agent startup; launch completes after the readiness probe succeeds.
  • Failures/deadlines roll back launch.
  • The default hook/probe deadline is 60 seconds, within the existing 180-second launch deadline.

  • Older images without the support label reject hooks.

  • Project [run] supports policy_preset, deny_read, deny_write, max_lifetime, idle_timeout, retention, argv arrays for start_hooks/readiness, and readiness_timeout.

  • Host secrets, extra mounts, runtime and proxy endpoints remain host settings.

docs.title: Credentials and compatibility
docs.text:
• oaiso proxy run --credential-routes /absolute/private-routes.json mounts a 0600 host JSON file read-only into the auth proxy alone.
  • The egress proxy remains credential-free.
  • Example values are synthetic:
[{"Name":"service","Upstream":"https://api.example.com","Paths":["/v1"],"Methods":["GET","POST"],"Header":"X-Service-Key","Prefix":"","Provider":"openai","Secret":"HOST_SECRET"}]
  • Guests send live placeholder Bearer tokens to http://AUTH_PROXY/broker/service/v1/....
  • Fixed HTTPS origin, path boundaries, method and provider are checked before injecting credentials.
  • Encoded paths, WebSockets and following upstream redirects are disallowed.
  • Secrets are never returned by a credential retrieval API.
  • Only configure trusted upstream APIs: an upstream that echoes its received secret can expose it.
  • Changes require drain/recreation.
  • Embedders can also use StartCredentialBroker with CredentialRoute.Secret callbacks, explicitly arranging listeners and worker network placement.
oaiso run --ssh-proxy --jvm-proxy --ca-bundle /absolute/extra-ca.pem -d
oaiso proxy run --upstream-proxy http://proxy.example.com:3128 --ca-bundle /absolute/extra-ca.pem
  • SSH uses a GIT_SSH_COMMAND CONNECT helper through the egress policy.
  • Host SSH keys/agent sockets are not shared automatically.
  • JVM HTTP(S) proxy properties are opt-in.
  • Worker CA bundles extend system trust for curl, Python and Node.
  • When Java and keytool are installed, the worker copies the system JVM truststore into its HOME and imports the additional certificates.
  • Proxy CA bundles extend system roots for both HTTP and WebSocket TLS verification.
  • Proxy chaining sends CONNECT to locally verified destination IPs and preserves private-IP blocking.
  • Credential-bearing upstream proxy URLs are rejected.

docs.title: Go API and performance
docs.text:
• The Go API adds Policy, ExplainPolicy, PolicyEvents, execution working directories/environments/TTY, StartSession/Resize, file and job operations, diff recovery and Reap.
  • Existing methods remain available.

  • Probe node and proxy capabilities separately.

  • The network-policy benchmark identified per-request linear domain scans and repeated IP parsing.

  • Compiled domain indexes preserve existing domain/IP matching semantics, covered by equivalence tests.
  • For 1000 domains, three runs on the same host measured 65.9–181 µs, 48112 B and 1002 allocations per check before, versus 152–153 ns, 0 B and 0 allocations after.
  • These are policy checks, not end-to-end network latency.
  • Reproduce with:
go test ./internal/networkpolicy -run '^$' -bench . -benchmem -count=3
  • TUI logs append incrementally instead of rebuilding history on each write, with 2000 lines and approximately 4 MiB per segment.
  • Polling stops when the UI exits.

The verification record distinguishes fixture tests, native Kata acceptance, and external-service tests.

docs.title: Model authorization and staged startup
docs.text:
• Use repeated oaiso proxy run --allow-model model-id, host [proxy].allowed_models, or CaseProxyOptions.AllowedModels to restrict a whole auth proxy to exact submitted model IDs.
  • Empty preserves legacy behavior.
  • The immutable configuration requires draining workers and recreating the proxy to change.

  • ProxyCapabilities reports support and active enforcement separately.

  • When enabled, authenticated POST requests are checked before credential injection or upstream I/O.

  • Only JSON bodies up to 8 MiB are accepted; duplicate keys, case variants of model, invalid JSON, compressed bodies and encoded paths are rejected.
  • The only allowed query is exact beta=true on Claude Messages/count_tokens; every other query is denied.
  • The original checked bytes are forwarded and redirects are not followed.
  • Supported paths are /v1/responses, /v1/responses/compact, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/moderations, /chatgpt/codex/responses, /chatgpt/codex/responses/compact, /anthropic/v1/messages, and /anthropic/v1/messages/count_tokens.
  • All other AI paths, model-listing/batch/file APIs and WebSockets are denied.
  • Clients must support HTTP.
  • This controls the submitted ID, not upstream alias resolution.

  • Custom broker routes, general egress and separately supplied credentials have separate policies; disable or restrict egress and do not configure alternative AI broker routes when model enforcement is mandatory.

  • Create materializes a Kata worker without starting a VM, hooks or agent or issuing a live worker token.

  • It still creates networks, snapshots and a host reservation; defer Create too if resource allocation requires approval.
  • Remove abandoned workers explicitly.
  • Maximum lifetime counts from creation, including any approval wait.
  • Create and Launch cannot share a request ID; retries of the same operation keep the same ID.
  • Start verifies isolation, activates the token and waits for hooks/readiness.
  • After cancellation or failure, reconcile with Request/Get and use a fresh context for cleanup.
  • Launch retains its combined behavior.

docs.title: Supervised collection and memory observation
docs.text:
• The optional systemd user unit deploy/kata/codex-dock-reaper.service runs the installed /usr/local/bin/oaiso reap --watch and restarts on failure after five seconds.
  • Copy it to ~/.config/systemd/user/, reload the user manager and explicitly enable/start the unit.
  • Monitor its journal and status.
  • An administrator must configure user linger if it needs to survive logout.
  • Nothing is enabled automatically.

  • Multi-case products should periodically call Reap through clients holding their own admin credentials and monitor failures.

  • Updated nodes protect pending execs, active exec/PTY sessions and detached jobs against idle collection, checking atomically with stopping so newly started work is protected too.

  • Main agent activity and work started outside the management API are not measured; disable idle limits for these workloads.

  • Explicit maximum lifetime still applies to busy workers.

  • ResourceUsage returns a verified running VM's host cgroup current memory, optional peak and OOM-kill count separately from guest/host capacity budgets.

  • These are not guest RSS.
  • The guest budget is the worker cgroup limit, separate from total VM RAM shown by /proc/meminfo.
  • The standard default and small guest 1 GiB / host 2 GiB profile remain unchanged.
  • An explicit compact profile provides guest 512 MiB / host 768 MiB, one CPU and 512 PIDs for lightweight tasks.
  • Select CLI --profile-size compact or Go Profile: "compact" after querying Profiles on an updated node.
  • This is not a guarantee that large dependency installs/builds fit; measure product-specific workloads, concurrency, peaks and OOM events.
  • CLI vm inspect --json exposes the same host observations.

docs.title: Operator resource profiles
docs.text:
• PID limits are configured per profile.
  • For example, oaiso profile define compact-256 --base compact --pids-limit 256 prints a JSON array with compact's CPU/memory budgets and a 256-PID ceiling.
  • It does not edit files or node configuration.
  • If definitions already exist, add the generated element to their array.
  • oaiso profile --node --json queries built-in and registered profiles on the running node; oaiso profile compact-256 --node displays one selected budget.

  • Without --node, the command continues to display built-in defaults.

  • Built-in standard, small and compact budgets are unchanged.

  • Operators can register additional CPU, guest/host memory and PID combinations in a root-owned JSON file with no group/world write permission.
  • Load it with node serve --resource-profiles /etc/codex-dock/resource-profiles.json:
[{"name":"batch","cpu_cores":2,"guest_memory_bytes":536870912,"host_memory_bytes":805306368,"pid_limit":256}]
  • Names start with a lowercase letter and contain lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, up to 63 characters.
  • The file permits 32 definitions and 64 KiB; duplicate or built-in names are rejected.
  • Bounds are 1–64 CPUs, 512–2048 MiB guest memory, host memory at least 256 MiB above guest memory and at most 3072 MiB, and 64–4096 PIDs.
  • Memory must be MiB-aligned.

  • These settings stay within pinned Dragonball assets and retain mandatory host/guest startup verification.

  • Query client.Profiles(ctx) before selecting Profile: "batch".

  • CLI callers use --profile-size batch or global run.profile_size; completion queries the node.

  • The package-level cxd.Profiles() returns built-in defaults only.

  • Non-512 PID profiles require the updated guest hook and schema-v2 metadata bound to that image.

  • prepare_guest.py build generates these assets; runtime-lock checks the image SHA256 and pins matching metadata as guest-policy.
  • Legacy images/manifests retain 512 behavior.
  • Registering non-512 limits on unsupported assets fails node startup.
  • Check dynamic-pid-profiles-v1 and operator-resource-profiles-v1.

  • The node sets an OCI annotation and bootstrap verifies the actual guest limit before activating credentials, using the pinned Kata hook state.

  • Drain existing VMs before switching/resealing guest images.

  • Allocation records pin the full custom budget.
  • Adding names does not change asset stamps, but file changes require a node restart.
  • Drain every reservation using a definition before modifying or deleting it: retained reservations cannot be reinterpreted.
  • Restore the old definition before recovery if it was changed accidentally.

  • Deployment and service restart are not automatic.

  • When resealing, use runtime-lock --logger /absolute/current/codex-dock-io-logger to select the matching logger explicitly.

  • An older helper selected through PATH may lack bounded-job logging options; pin the matching node-bundle helper.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
日本語 | English

Boundary Implementation Worker isolation Separate guest kernel with Kata runtime-rs / Dragonball Admission Root node verifies assets, host processes and resource limits before releasing user code Failed checks Stop startup; no fallback to runc or QEMU

docs.title: Worker boundary
docs.text:
Control Default User Non-root; caller's UID/GID Capabilities All sets cleared Guest restrictions NoNewPrivs=1, Seccomp=2 Guest resources 1 CPU, 2 GiB memory, 512 PIDs Host VM envelope 1 CPU, 3 GiB memory, no swap, 512 PIDs Network No direct internet, host or peer access; selected proxies only Management No node/containerd/BuildKit sockets or allocation records in workers
  • Verified Kata workers: Codex's inner sandbox uses danger-full-access to avoid nested namespace/seccomp conflicts.
  • Agent approval settings remain separate.
  • Shared files remain accessible under the selected mount permissions.

docs.title: Storage and worker-visible fields
docs.text: Information Handling Real API keys and OAuth access/refresh/ID tokens Retained by the auth proxy; never returned to workers Worker credentials Short-lived placeholders Codex ID field Fresh dummy JWT: account ID, plan and FedRAMP flag only Original JWT headers/signature, email, user IDs and arbitrary claims Never forwarded Dummy JWT Client metadata only; not used for upstream authentication Egress proxy Receives no real credentials

docs.title: Acquisition, refresh and existing workers
docs.text:
• Initial acquisition and refresh return only selected fields.
  • Refresh errors retain HTTP status and known CLI recovery codes.
  • Issuer bodies and transport error details are not forwarded.
  • Tests: pinned CLI verification (Japanese).
  • Existing files/logs are not automatically erased: update the proxy, then stop and recreate old workers.

docs.title: Files and mounts
docs.text:
Item Contract Legacy auth files Caller UID/GID, private HOME, read-only mounts; owner-only 0600 retained Independent profiles No host auth mounts/environment; only the selected 0700 directory mounted read-write for refresh Credentials and lock files 0600; CAS, fsync and atomic rename Worker restart Verify profile and connection generation Capabilities and source modes No added capabilities or source-permission changes Admin authority Optional separate 0600 file, read-only mount into auth only; value stays out of argv Worker shares CLI rejects profile-storage overlaps; embedding callers must also keep credentials/admin authority outside shares At-rest encryption New development login profiles default to Secret Service plus age/HMAC-SHA256; explicit passphrase mode remains available. No ciphertext or keys in work VMs
  • Trusted control environments may run inside WSL or a Linux VM.
  • Untrusted work VMs must never receive real credentials.
  • Requirements and deployment checks: WSL, VMs and headless systems.

docs.title: Encryption limits
docs.text:
• Protect inactive credential files; host root/same-UID process access, live memory, swap and outer VM snapshots are outside this protection.
  • Never store a passphrase alongside ciphertext. Lost keys require reauthentication.
  • Unlock failure never switches to host credentials, plaintext or another backend. Coexisting migration records fail closed.
  • Keyring storage encryption/locking depend on OS configuration.
  • Usage, specification, verification gaps.

docs.title: Token and admin boundaries
docs.text: Condition Behavior HTTP / WebSocket AI requests Validate issued, unexpired token before contacting upstream Revocation, expiry or replacement Cancel active streams and tunnels Admin operations Separate listener, unreachable from worker networks

docs.title: Trusted host operators
docs.text:
Item Trust or verification Node socket / BuildKit access Root-equivalent; operators choose images, commands and host mounts Runtime assets, tools and configuration Pinned in a root-owned manifest Manifest Does not replace release provenance or checksum verification Asset validation Reread and hash every asset on every validation Parallel readers At most GOMAXPROCS and four readers per validation Timestamp cache Never used to skip verification cgroup.kill recovery Verify all occupants of a dedicated resource group first Other processes Do not adopt arbitrary PIDs or other products' VMs

Measurement guide

docs.title: Communication and authorization
docs.text:
Item Limit or default Worker-to-proxy traffic Plain HTTP on dedicated networks; no TLS Bearer tokens No source container-ID attestation General egress Default deny unless the host explicitly disables it Empty destination grants Disconnect general egress Worker-specific allowlists Select policy-specific proxies; identical policies can share Rule updates Immutable per proxy; no hot reload Model authorization Opt-in at the host auth proxy; a CLI model flag alone does not enforce authorization Shared files / Git metadata Remain writable where explicitly shared read-write
  • Model routes, WebSocket denial and separate paths: additional controls.

docs.title: Quarantine
docs.text:
Operation or condition Effect policy quarantine / Go API Quarantine Stop one worker and durably prohibit restart at the node Work terminated Jobs, general communication and AI communication Workspace Retained; create a new worker to resume under new rules Error Does not establish completed isolation; retry

Quarantine semantics

docs.title: Verification scope
docs.text:
Status Coverage Recorded real Kata / AI tests (Japanese) Real Kata acceptance and existing-auth.json WebSocket/HTTP SSE inference Requires separate verification Long-running real OAuth refresh, interactive keyboard use, arbitrary custom images Claude fixture coverage Distinct API/subscription placeholders; no real access/refresh tokens in workers Outside Claude fixture coverage Live Anthropic inference and subscription usage accounting Ongoing maintenance Host kernel, KVM, Kata and guest kernel updates

Claude Code · Acceptance record (Japanese)

docs.title: Static upstream contract checks
docs.text:
• The development-only checker detects changes to Codex, Claude Code, public APIs, SDK types and authentication-related sources using deterministic rules.
  • It does not change worker execution, proxy behavior or credentials.
  • It does not run login, inference, OAuth refresh, tools or Kata acceptance.
  • See testing for those checks.

docs.title: Monitored contracts
docs.text:
compat/upstream/manifest.json selects the contracts; compat/upstream/baseline.json stores the reference observation.

Source Selected declarations OpenAI OpenAPI POST /responses, /responses/compact, /chat/completions, /completions, /embeddings, /moderations, including referenced types, security and servers Codex config Provider selection/definitions, ChatGPT URL and the app/compression/WebSocket flags used by this product Codex CLI Root/exec help, including required flags and their signatures/help Codex app-server Generated Initialize, ThreadStart, TurnStart and TurnInterrupt schemas OpenAI SDK Responses request and stream-event declarations Codex authentication Fingerprints of upstream OAuth storage and refresh source files Claude Code CLI Root/auth-status help, including required flags and their signatures/help Anthropic SDK Messages/count_tokens request and stream-event declarations Claude Agent SDK Public Python SDK annotations and type aliases Claude authentication Fingerprint of official CHANGELOG lines mentioning OAuth, credentials, login and related terms
  • Floating GitHub refs are resolved to commit SHAs once per repository/ref per capture.
  • Snapshots record immutable source URLs, original artifact hashes, capture time and actual CLI versions.
  • Tracked branch observations and CLI releases are separate.
  • The initial CLI baseline matches the worker image: Codex 0.163.0 and Claude Code 2.1.306.
  • Recording a baseline does not certify upstream source correctness or live compatibility.

docs.title: Baseline storage
docs.text:
• The versioned baseline is a compact schema 2 source lock.
  • Eleven public API/SDK/auth sources retain immutable commit URLs, raw artifact SHA256 hashes and normalized contract SHA256 hashes.
  • Three CLI-generated sources (Codex/Claude help and Codex app-server schemas) retain their comparison data because an immutable public URL cannot reliably reproduce those outputs.

  • The initial baseline shrank from 1.29 MB / 43,255 lines to approximately 92 KB / 2,425 lines.

  • capture still writes a complete schema 1 candidate.

  • compare restores reference contracts from an unchanged candidate, a verified cache, or the pinned URL, in that order, then performs the same structural comparison.
  • Both hashes are checked for cached or downloaded data.
  • It never substitutes latest sources: an unavailable or mismatching reference produces error (exit 2).

  • Changed sources require network access when their reference is not cached.

  • The default cache is the Git-ignored .kata-verification/upstream-contract-cache; override it with compare --cache-dir PATH.

  • CI caches restored references to reduce repeated downloads.
  • The cache and 30-day artifacts are optional helpers; the versioned lock defines the baseline.
  • Restoration without a cache depends on the upstream pinned URL remaining available.
  • Complete schema 1 baselines remain supported.
  • The compact format currently supports GitHub commit URLs.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Level Examples Result breaking Selected flag/operation/property removed, type changed, required request field added, required response field removed Hold review Security/server change, SDK declaration change, changed composition or unknown constraints, authentication source/release-note drift Hold info Optional property added, unused flag changed, CLI version changed, request enum widened Record error Fetch/parse failure, unresolved reference, missing source or manifest mismatch Inspection failed
  • Required-field and enum comparisons account for request/response direction.
  • Local schema references and cycles are followed.
  • External references fail inspection.
  • Descriptions/examples and some ordering differences are ignored.

  • Unproven compatibility is held conservatively.

  • App-server, OpenAI SDK and Claude Agent SDK sources are advisory because this product does not directly interpret their public types.

  • Their breaking differences become review, rather than claiming a demonstrated runtime failure.
  • Coverage is limited to the operations, files and flags selected in the manifest; SDK imports are not recursively scanned.

docs.title: Run locally
docs.text:
• Use Python 3.12 or later.
  • Offline rule tests and baseline/worker-pin validation:
make contracts-check
  • To fetch upstream declarations, install the YAML development dependency and stage CLIs without updating global installations.
  • Change the npm version selectors to inspect other candidates.
python3 -m pip install -r requirements-contracts.txt
npm install --prefix .kata-verification/contracts-tools --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund \
  @openai/codex@0.163.0 @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.306
node .kata-verification/contracts-tools/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/install.cjs
python3 scripts/upstream-contracts.py capture \
  --codex .kata-verification/contracts-tools/node_modules/.bin/codex \
  --claude .kata-verification/contracts-tools/node_modules/.bin/claude \
  --out .kata-verification/contracts/candidate.json
python3 scripts/upstream-contracts.py compare \
  --candidate .kata-verification/contracts/candidate.json \
  --json .kata-verification/contracts/report.json \
  --markdown .kata-verification/contracts/report.md
  • install.cjs selects the platform executable for native Claude releases; omit that step for older packages without it.
  • CLI inspection uses a new HOME/config directory and an environment allowlist.
  • Host API keys, OAuth variables, login files and SSH agents are not passed.

  • The official CLI's help/version/schema code still executes: inspect trusted distributions in a dedicated environment.

  • compare exits with 0 for informational changes only, 1 for a hold and 2 for inspection failure.

  • Report status is pass, hold or error.
  • Partial capture failures are saved in the candidate JSON.

docs.title: CI and baseline maintenance
docs.text:
• Normal CI runs offline rule tests and validates lock URLs, hash formats, embedded CLI contracts, the manifest and worker Dockerfile CLI pins.
  • This offline check does not download or verify public artifact contents.

  • Changing a worker CLI pin without updating its baseline fails validation.

  • The read-only Upstream static contracts workflow runs daily or manually against latest upstream declarations and candidate CLIs.

  • Manual runs accept CLI version selectors.
  • Reports appear in the Actions summary and artifacts retained for 30 days.
  • Review/breaking findings and inspection failures fail the job.

  • It does not automatically update baselines, images or operating configuration, or create PRs.

  • Update the baseline only when adopting reviewed CLI or contract changes.

  • Daily inspection does not create Git changes.

  • Upstream change frequency has not been measured; broad SDK type definitions may generate findings more frequently than CLI adoption.

  • Review the precise changes and immutable sources, make required fixes, then run appropriate compatibility tests.

  • Convert the reviewed full candidate to a compact lock and commit it:
python3 scripts/upstream-contracts.py compact \
  --snapshot .kata-verification/contracts/candidate.json \
  --out compat/upstream/baseline.json
make contracts-check
  • Update worker pins when adopting a CLI.
  • A manifest change requires explicit coverage review and recapture.
  • Snapshots from a different manifest are rejected.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Server-only changes to revocation, concurrent refresh, authorization, errors or stream disconnection require behavioral tests.
  • Claude subscription refresh has no public schema monitored here.
  • Unannounced changes and files outside the manifest are not covered.
  • Authentication fingerprints can also flag comment-only changes.
  • pass only means no blocking monitored static drift; it does not certify live API/subscription operation or overall security.

Official references

Component Reference OpenAI OpenAPI OpenAI OpenAPI Codex schema generation Codex schema generation Claude CLI Claude CLI Anthropic SDKs Anthropic SDKs

docs.title: Administration
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Prerequisite: an installed execution host.
  • Operational procedures below are currently available in Japanese; the performance guide is also in English.

docs.title: Daily operations
docs.text: Task Guide List workers, follow logs, stop, restart and remove Operations (Japanese), worker commands Inspect VM ownership and remaining resources VM management (Japanese) Inspect or manage workers interactively TUI

docs.title: Host maintenance
docs.text:
Task Guide Update an automatically installed node Host installation and updates (Japanese) Install or maintain a host manually Kata host setup (Japanese) Migrate a legacy installation Migration (Japanese) Diagnose startup, credentials or networking Troubleshooting (Japanese) Compare performance and reproduce benchmarks Performance
  • Save work before maintenance; follow the linked procedure to drain and reclaim workers.
  • Normal worker commands run as the operator; host installation uses administrator privileges.

docs.title: Auth API
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • See overview and tokens.
  • These routes belong to the auth role.
  • The egress role provides forwarding and health only.

docs.title: Listeners
docs.text:
Listener Default URL Caller Data http://codex-auth-proxy:18080 Workers Admin http://127.0.0.1:18081 Host CLI
  • proxy run separates admin from data.
  • For a custom proxy serve, specify --admin-listen.
  • If an admin secret is configured, /admin/* requires X-Proxy-Admin-Secret.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
Method Path Authentication / purpose GET /token X-Codex-Token; obtain placeholders POST /oauth/token ?cdx=<worker token>; OpenAI refresh ANY / WS /v1/*, /chatgpt/* Bearer worker token ANY / WS /anthropic/* x-api-key or Bearer worker token GET /health No authentication; process health POST /revoke Legacy data-plane revocation; prefer /admin/revoke POST /admin/issue Issue token POST /admin/restore Restore saved placeholder POST /admin/revoke Revoke token GET /admin/mode Authentication modes and capability
  • Independent profiles set independent_profile true and return their name and login generation in admin-only X-Cxd-Auth-Profile / X-Cxd-Connection-Version headers.
  • case_proxy denotes external cases and remains false for local profiles.
  • These fields contain no real credentials.
  • Profiles require a separate admin listener and an admin secret of at least 32 bytes.

docs.title: GET /token
docs.text:
• Send X-Codex-Token: cdx-<64 hexadecimal digits>.
  • Returns 200 JSON in API-key mode:
{"api_key": "cdx-<64 hexadecimal digits>", "container_name": "worker-name"}

OAuth mode returns:

{
  "oauth_access_token": "cdx-<64 hexadecimal digits>",
  "oauth_id_token": "<dummy JWT containing selected account metadata>",
  "oauth_account_id": "<account ID>",
  "oauth_last_refresh": "<timestamp>",
  "container_name": "worker-name"
}
  • The API/access token is the submitted placeholder.
  • Real access/refresh/ID tokens are not returned.
  • The ID field is a fresh dummy JWT containing only account ID, plan and the FedRAMP flag, without the original signature or arbitrary claims.
  • Successful responses set Cache-Control: no-store.
  • Invalid, missing or expired tokens return 401; wrong methods return 405.

docs.title: POST /oauth/token
docs.text:
• OpenAI refresh relay used by CODEX_REFRESH_TOKEN_URL_OVERRIDE.
  • Authenticate with ?cdx=<worker token> because the client does not attach custom refresh headers.
{"client_id": "<client ID>", "grant_type": "refresh_token", "refresh_token": ""}
  • The proxy substitutes the real host refresh token before forwarding to OpenAI.
  • Success responses contain only access_token (the worker placeholder) and id_token (fresh dummy JWT).
  • Refresh tokens and arbitrary issuer fields are not returned.
  • Real updated credentials are persisted on the proxy side.
  • Upstream error status is preserved; the body becomes {"error":"<code>"}.
  • Only refresh_token_expired, refresh_token_reused, refresh_token_invalidated and invalid_grant are retained in canonical lowercase; other codes become oauth_refresh_failed.
  • Issuer messages and reflected credentials are never forwarded.
  • Success and upstream-error responses set Cache-Control: no-store.

Errors: 400 for wrong mode or malformed request, 401 for invalid worker token, 405 for wrong method, 502 for upstream connection failure.

docs.title: AI HTTP and WebSocket routes
docs.text:
• /v1/* and /chatgpt/* require Authorization: Bearer <worker token>.
  • /anthropic/* accepts x-api-key or Bearer.
  • If both are present they must match.
  • Missing, unissued, expired, revoked, duplicate or conflicting credentials return 401 before an upstream connection.
  • Expiry, revocation and replacement cancel existing HTTP streams and WS tunnels.
Route / mode Upstream /v1/*, API key https://api.openai.com/v1/* /v1/*, ChatGPT OAuth https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/* /chatgpt/* https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/* /anthropic/* https://api.anthropic.com/*
  • Worker authentication is removed and real provider credentials are injected.
  • ChatGPT account ID is overwritten with the correct value.
  • HTTP hop-by-hop headers are removed; upstream status/body and relevant headers are returned.
  • SSE is streamed and validated WebSockets are tunneled.

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text:
{"status": "ok", "active_tokens": 3}
  • The count is in-memory records, which can include expired records awaiting cleanup.
  • This is not a proof of token validity or upstream AI connectivity.

docs.title: Admin API
docs.text:
• If configured, supply X-Proxy-Admin-Secret: <secret> on all admin calls.
  • Wrong secrets return 401 and wrong methods return 405.

docs.title: POST /admin/issue
docs.text:
{"container": "worker-name", "ttl": 3600}
  • container is required.
  • An omitted or nonpositive TTL uses the proxy default.
  • Returns 200 with {"token": "cdx-..."}.
  • Invalid JSON or an empty name returns 400.
  • Issuing for the same name cancels the previous lease and connections.

docs.title: POST /admin/restore
docs.text:
{"container": "worker-name", "token": "cdx-<64 hexadecimal digits>", "ttl": 3600}
  • Reactivates a saved placeholder; success is 204.
  • Invalid name/format/TTL or a token assigned to another worker returns 400.
  • Real API keys are not accepted.
  • Managed restart handles this automatically.

docs.title: POST /admin/revoke
docs.text:
• Specify ?container=worker-name.
  • Success is 200; missing name is 400.
  • Cancels the lease and its connections.
  • Legacy POST /revoke uses the same query but does not validate an admin secret; use the separated admin route for management tools.

docs.title: GET /admin/mode
docs.text:
{
  "oauth_mode": true,
  "anthropic_available": false,
  "anthropic_oauth_mode": false,
  "worker_token_auth": true
}
  • Current clients reject proxies without worker_token_auth: true.
  • Rebuild and recreate old proxies before creating workers.
  • See operations (Japanese).

docs.title: Short-lived tokens
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • A cdx-... value is a bearer token for the proxy, not a real provider API key.
  • Anyone holding a valid token can use the AI proxy routes until it expires or is revoked.

docs.title: Format and lifetime
docs.text:
• Tokens use 32 cryptographically random bytes, encoded as 64 hexadecimal characters after cdx- (68 characters total).
  • The default TTL is 3600 seconds.
oaiso run --agent codex --token-ttl 7200
  • Expired tokens are rejected immediately and their active HTTP/WS connections are canceled.
  • The 30-second record cleanup loop does not delay authentication expiry.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Action Result Create worker Issue and activate before releasing user code Stop Revoke token and cancel active connections Restart Restore the saved placeholder and release code after Kata checks Reissue or restore for the same name Cancel the previous lease and connections Remove Revoke and reclaim resources; retain retry records on failure Stop proxy Revoke all tokens and connections; issuance records are in memory
  • Use oaiso start NAME to restart a stopped worker.
  • The admin restore API accepts saved placeholders, not real API keys or another worker's token.

docs.title: Worker data
docs.text:
• CODEX_TOKEN and CODEX_AUTH_PROXY_URL bootstrap authentication and are unset by the entrypoint.
  • Client files still retain placeholders.
  • API-key variables contain placeholders.
  • OAuth auth.json has a placeholder access token, an empty refresh token and a fresh dummy ID JWT containing only account ID, plan and the FedRAMP flag.
  • Real ID tokens remain on the host.
  • Codex configuration points requests to the proxy.
  • CODEX_REFRESH_TOKEN_URL_OVERRIDE includes the worker token.
  • Paths depend on the selected user's HOME, not a fixed /home/codex.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• All HTTP/WS AI routes validate issued, unexpired tokens and reject duplicate or conflicting authentication.
  • There is no source container-ID attestation.
  • Worker-to-proxy traffic is plain HTTP on dedicated networks.
  • Choose a TTL suitable for the task and revoke unused tokens by stopping or removing workers.

See API reference and security.

docs.title: oaiso auth — Authentication Management
docs.text:
日本語 | English

← Command Reference

Goal Command or setting Store a product-specific API key auth profile set NAME --provider openai\|anthropic Import OAuth credentials auth profile import NAME --credentials-stdin --format codex\|claude\|credentials Inspect redacted metadata auth profile show NAME / auth profile list Select a profile --auth-profile NAME or global auth_profile Keep legacy host integration Leave profiles unselected; use auth show / auth set

docs.title: Keyring
docs.text:
• oaiso auth keyring check: store/read/delete probe without displaying secrets.
  • oaiso auth keyring session [-- COMMAND...]: private headless session.
  • Dependencies, unlocking and session lifetime.

docs.title: Behavior and storage
docs.text: Item Contract Separation Never automatically reuse host CLI logins or authentication variables Missing profile or unsafe permissions Fail; never fall back to host credentials Example file ~/.config/codex-dock/profiles/work/work.json Root and profile directories 0700 JSON and lock files 0600, plaintext Override the root --auth-profile-dir or trusted global auth_profile_dir WSL Private Linux-side storage, outside shared/synced folders Input No keys in arguments; noninteractive input requires explicit stdin

docs.title: Register an API key
docs.text:
oaiso auth profile set work --provider openai  # hidden TTY input
oaiso auth profile set claude-work --provider anthropic
oaiso auth profile show work
oaiso auth profile list
  • Interactive: hidden TTY input.
  • Noninteractive: --key-stdin with a protected input source.
  • This command only saves the key. Development-version login also checks the live API connection during registration.
  • Success: Profile created (plaintext, 0600). See the profile inspection example.

docs.title: Import OAuth
docs.text:
oaiso auth profile import work-oauth --format codex --credentials-stdin < /private/product-login/auth.json
oaiso auth profile import claude-oauth --format claude --credentials-stdin < /private/product-login/.credentials.json
--format Input codex Native tokens and last_refresh claude claudeAiOauth credentials (default) credentialstore.Credentials JSON; can contain both providers
  • --credentials-stdin: required.
  • Source files: never automatically discovered or deleted.
  • This command explicitly imports existing JSON. Development-version login authenticates through a dedicated Kata.
  • Success: Profile imported (plaintext, 0600). Check for oauth on the registered provider's line.

docs.title: Create admin authority and start the proxy
docs.text:
• Store admin authority in a separate 0600 file.
  • Pass its path, keeping the secret value out of process arguments.
  • The generator refuses to overwrite an existing file; skip generation when reusing an existing secret.
  • Run on the host, outside the worker.
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, pathlib, secrets
path = pathlib.Path.home() / '.config/codex-dock/proxy-admin-secret'
path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
with os.fdopen(os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600), 'w') as f:
    f.write(secrets.token_hex(32) + '\n')
PY
  • Successful generation produces no output. Check only permissions and location:
stat -c '%a %n' "$HOME/.config/codex-dock/proxy-admin-secret"

600 /home/user/.config/codex-dock/proxy-admin-secret
  • /home/user is replaced by your HOME. You do not need to display the secret contents.

docs.title: Fix the selection for daily operations
docs.text:
Location: trusted global ~/.config/codex-dock/config.toml.

  • Create the file if absent; merge these keys into existing settings without replacing unrelated values.
  • Put auth_profile before the first table, such as [run] or [proxy].
  • If [proxy] already exists, add admin_secret_file there; do not duplicate the table.
  • Replace work and /home/user/... with the real profile name and absolute path; do not assume $HOME or ~ expands inside TOML.
auth_profile = "work"
[proxy]
admin_secret_file = "/home/user/.config/codex-dock/proxy-admin-secret"
Command Selection or output init, run, start, TUI Share the global settings above oaiso run Also accepts explicit profile flags oaiso codex / oaiso claude Forward arguments to the agent; select profiles through global settings auth show Redacted metadata for the selected profile
  • Never put authentication configuration in the project's oaiso.toml.

After configuring, run one preparation command as your normal user (any directory for release installations):

Stored credentials Preparation OpenAI oaiso init --agent codex Anthropic oaiso init --agent claude
  • Then change to your project and run oaiso codex or oaiso claude.
  • An explicit one-off invocation is oaiso --auth-profile work run --agent codex --proxy-admin-secret-file "$HOME/.config/codex-dock/proxy-admin-secret". These flags do not carry over to later stop, start or TUI commands; use global settings for daily operations.

docs.title: Refresh, switching and sharing
docs.text:
Operation or boundary Behavior Creation/import Create-only; never overwrite an existing profile Normal OAuth refresh CAS-save to the same Store; preserve connection generation Re-login Import under a new profile name Retained workers No reauthorization under another profile or login generation Auth proxy Only the selected directory is mounted read-write for refresh Workers and egress Never receive credential storage Workspaces and extra mounts Must exclude credential storage and admin-secret files

Switch after re-login

  1. Create/import a new profile name.
  2. Stop and remove old workers.
  3. With the old settings, run oaiso proxy stop, then oaiso proxy rm.
  4. Change global auth_profile to the new name.
  5. Run init for the selected agent as your normal user to recreate the proxy.

  6. Create new workers from the project directory.

  7. The following legacy commands apply without profile selection.

  8. Profile mode rejects legacy auth set / auth rotate.

docs.title: auth show
docs.text:
oaiso auth show
  • Shows the current authentication source.
  • Never displays actual keys or tokens.
  • Without profile selection, reports legacy OpenAI metadata only; it does not check Anthropic credentials.
  • This metadata does not establish the running proxy's selected mode or successful live authentication.
  • With both legacy OpenAI OAuth and an API key present, display precedence differs from proxy selection; check the runtime precedence.
Auth source: OPENAI_API_KEY env
Key configured: true

docs.title: auth set
docs.text:
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
oaiso auth set
Item Value Source OPENAI_API_KEY Destination ~/.config/codex-dock/apikey Permissions 0600 Condition No independent profile selected

docs.title: auth rotate
docs.text:
oaiso auth rotate
Goal Operation Write a local update marker auth rotate; does not immediately revoke a running proxy's tokens Revoke immediately Stop the worker or use /admin/revoke Update the proxy Operations (Japanese)

docs.title: Related Documentation
docs.text: Topic Guide Source precedence and credential protection Auth proxy Configuration values and files Configuration Initial setup Quick start

docs.title: Encrypted storage (development)
docs.text:
• Backends and operation; unavailable in published v0.0.2.
  • New: oaiso login --encrypt / --keyring.
  • Migrate plaintext: oaiso auth profile encrypt NAME.
  • Migrate legacy ciphertext to age: oaiso auth profile migrate-age NAME.
  • Change passphrase: oaiso auth profile passwd NAME.
  • Stop affected workers/proxies and lock: oaiso auth profile lock NAME.
  • Metadata inspection neither decrypts nor displays secrets.

docs.title: Build images
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • oaiso build uses standalone BuildKit and imports OCI output into the worker's containerd namespace.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
oaiso build
oaiso build --template list
oaiso build --template pwn
oaiso build -f ./Dockerfile --tag my-codex:v1
oaiso run --image my-codex:v1
Option Purpose --tag, -t Image tag; normally codex-dock:latest, or the selected template's tag --dockerfile, -f Dockerfile path --template, -T Template name, or list --print-entrypoint Print embedded entrypoint.sh and exit without building
  • The built-in worker pins Codex CLI with CODEX_CLI_VERSION in its Dockerfile.
  • To test another exact version, build a separate OCI image in the worker's containerd namespace:
CODEX_DOCK_CODEX_VERSION=0.163.0 oaiso build --template plain --tag codex-dock:codex-0.163.0
oaiso image check codex-dock:codex-0.163.0 --agent codex
oaiso run --image codex-dock:codex-0.163.0 --agent codex
  • --template and -f are mutually exclusive.
  • Missing images are built from the corresponding template or default Dockerfile.
  • Build arbitrary custom tags explicitly before using them.
  • With a [build] section in the project's oaiso.toml, build, init, and run use the same build source.
  • Missing images are built after a fresh clone.

  • See project settings.

  • Claude Code is pinned with CLAUDE_CLI_VERSION=2.1.306.

  • Use CODEX_DOCK_CLAUDE_VERSION to override it for a build.
  • See Claude Code for image/proxy updates and verification.

docs.title: Custom image
docs.text:
• First build the base image with oaiso build.
  • Create this Dockerfile in a new working directory:
FROM codex-dock:latest
USER root
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends jq \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
USER codex

Then build and run it from that directory:

oaiso build -f ./Dockerfile --tag my-codex:jq
oaiso run --image my-codex:jq -- jq --version
  • The image inherits the agents and auth entrypoint.
  • Root is used for the build step; the Kata worker runs with a resolved non-root UID and verified restrictions.
  • Do not include credentials or management sockets in images.

docs.title: Independent base image
docs.text:
• Install the selected agent and entrypoint dependencies, using docker/sandbox/Dockerfile as the reference.
  • Get the matching entrypoint from your CLI:
oaiso build --print-entrypoint > entrypoint.sh

After creating the non-root user and installing dependencies, include:

COPY entrypoint.sh /entrypoint.sh
RUN chmod +x /entrypoint.sh
USER codex
WORKDIR /workspace
ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]
  • Refresh the entrypoint when updating the CLI.
  • Custom images pass the same Kata startup gate and need their own compatibility checks.

docs.title: User templates
docs.text:
• Place a Dockerfile at ~/.config/codex-dock/templates/<name>/Dockerfile.
  • User templates override built-ins with the same name.
mkdir -p ~/.config/codex-dock/templates/mytool
cp Dockerfile ~/.config/codex-dock/templates/mytool/Dockerfile
oaiso build --template mytool
oaiso run --template mytool
  • plain uses codex-dock:latest; other names use codex-dock:<name>.
  • make install-templates copies built-ins without overwriting existing files.
  • See auto_build.

docs.title: Build context
docs.text:
• With explicit -f, the context is the current directory.
  • Otherwise the search order is ./Dockerfile, ./docker/sandbox/Dockerfile, ./docker/Dockerfile, then ~/.config/codex-dock/Dockerfile.
  • The selected Dockerfile directory becomes the context.
  • Missing config defaults are generated.
  • Template builds create a temporary context with required entrypoint files.
  • Proxy images use proxy build.

docs.title: Builder connection
docs.text:
• The default address is unix:///run/codex-dock-buildkit/buildkitd.sock; override with BUILDKIT_HOST.
  • Use the dedicated containerd socket and namespace for BuildKit's containerd worker.
  • Proxy environment variables are passed as build args.
  • CODEX_PROXY_CERT is supplied as the proxy_ca secret, used only during RUN in built-in Dockerfiles.
  • Configure BuildKit daemon registry proxy/CA access separately.

docs.title: oaiso completion — shell completion
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • oaiso can generate completion scripts for Bash, Zsh, Fish, and PowerShell.
  • The release installer with --apply installs Bash, Zsh and Fish completion in the standard system directories.
  • Source installations also install completion through scripts/install.sh --apply or make install.
  • Open a new shell to use them.

  • Bash requires the bash-completion package.

  • Completion is generated and installed only for oaiso.

For the current Bash session:

source <(oaiso completion bash)
  • For Zsh, run autoload -Uz compinit; compinit before source <(oaiso completion zsh).

  • For Fish, run oaiso completion fish | source.

  • If you installed only the CLI with go install, you can save the script in your user's completion directory.

  • For Bash:
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions
oaiso completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/oaiso
  • Completion covers commands and flags, agent choices for default, agent/runtime/approval/template/--image values for run, and worker names for start, stop, rm, and logs.
  • For vm inspect/start/stop/rm, candidates come from the dedicated node's VM inventory and reflect the action.
  • Completion uses VM names when unambiguous and IDs for duplicate names or orphans.
  • Worker lookups have a 500 ms deadline; VM inventory lookups have a 2 second deadline.
  • Other completion remains available if the node is stopped.

docs.title: Removed firewall command
docs.text:
• oaiso firewall has been removed.
  • See current network controls.

docs.title: Login and first authentication setup
docs.text:
日本語 | English

Development version only. Published v0.0.2 uses manual independent profile setup.

  • Keyring storage is the default. On headless hosts, first open oaiso auth keyring session. Setup and use.

docs.title: Interactive login
docs.text:
oaiso login
  1. Choose codex or claude.
  2. Choose subscription or api-key.
  3. Follow the authentication instructions.
  4. Save a new independent profile and select it in global settings.
Method Behavior API key Hidden input followed by an official models-list API check; no inference request Subscription Official pinned CLI login in a dedicated Kata; no host CLI installation or login required

docs.title: Specify agent and method
docs.text:
oaiso login --agent codex --method subscription
oaiso login --agent claude --method subscription
oaiso login --agent claude --method api-key --profile work
  • Choose one example. An omitted profile name is generated; existing profiles are never overwritten.
  • Open the displayed URL in your browser and follow the official CLI. Codex uses a device code; Claude uses a URL and, when needed, a pasted code.
  • Account and organization settings determine subscription eligibility.
Flag Behavior --agent codex\|claude Select agent --method api-key\|subscription Authentication method --profile NAME New profile name --key-stdin Explicit API key input; requires agent and method flags --skip-check Explicitly save an unverified API key, for example offline --encrypt Encrypt directly with a hidden passphrase --keyring Secret Service encryption; the default for new login profiles --plaintext Explicit 0600 plaintext storage; mutually exclusive with --encrypt and --keyring --no-select Save without changing global settings

docs.title: Saved and connection-checked are different
docs.text:
Profile saved: work (encrypted, 0600).
Connection check: passed. Inference: not tested.
Selected profile: work
Settings: /home/user/.config/codex-dock/config.toml
  • Names and paths are examples. New login profiles use the keyring by default; use oaiso auth keyring session on headless hosts. Existing profiles are unchanged.
  • A passed models-list check does not establish inference success or permission to use every model.
  • Subscriptions report Official CLI login: completed. Inference: not tested.
  • Normal errors do not include upstream response bodies or real keys.

docs.title: Automatic setup
docs.text:
• Create the independent profile and owner-only storage.
  • Generate an owner-only admin-secret file if no admin authority is configured.
  • Select global auth_profile and the required admin-secret setting.
  • Retain existing network policy, unrelated settings and comments.
  • Never automatically remove or replace existing profiles, admin authority, workers or proxies.
  • If selection fails, retain the saved profile; retry with oaiso auth profile use NAME.

docs.title: Dedicated login Kata
docs.text:
• Retain the Kata attestation gate, non-root identity and resource limits.
  • No workspace, host HOME/authentication, user templates or project hooks.
  • Use the embedded recipe's fixed official CLIs, ignoring development CLI-version environment overrides.
  • Read-only image root; credentials live in a guest tmpfs limited to 128 MiB.
  • Dedicated credential-free egress restricted to authentication domains and port 443.
  • Login and collection use streaming exec, outside persistent console logs.
  • Remove the VM and dedicated egress on success, cancellation or failure. Report cleanup failure with a recoverable ID.
  • Stopped login sessions cannot be resumed; start a new login.
  • Ordinary work VMs continue to receive only short-lived placeholders through the Auth Proxy.

docs.title: Continue
docs.text:
oaiso init --agent claude
cd /path/to/your-project
oaiso claude
  • Replace both occurrences of claude with codex for Codex.
  • Drain old workers/proxies before initializing a different profile.
  • Official instructions: Codex authentication, Claude authentication.

docs.title: oaiso network — Network Management
docs.text:
日本語 | English

← Command Reference

  • Manages the egress network (dock-net-proxy, used for the proxy's internet reachability).
  • Per-worker Internal networks are created and removed automatically with each worker, so no manual management is needed.

The old oaiso firewall (iptables) command has been removed; isolation is enforced by the root node service with Linux bridges, namespaces and nftables.

docs.title: network create
docs.text:
oaiso network create

Also auto-created by oaiso proxy run if missing.

docs.title: network rm
docs.text:
oaiso network rm

Stop/remove the proxy container first if it is still attached.

docs.title: network status
docs.text:
oaiso network status

Egress network:  dock-net-proxy
  ID:            a1b2c3d4e5f6
  Driver:        bridge
  Internal:      false
  Subnet:        10.253.0.0/24
Worker networks: 2 (Internal, one per worker)
  - dock-net-w-codex-brave-otter
  - dock-net-w-codex-calm-finch

docs.title: Related Documentation
docs.text: • Network Specification

docs.title: Manage proxies
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • oaiso proxy manages the auth and general egress proxies on containerd.

  • See auth proxy and update procedure (Japanese).

  • Release installations prepare required images from the installed static CLI during init / proxy run. Ordinary use does not require proxy build, a source checkout or Go.

docs.title: Start
docs.text:
oaiso proxy run
Flag Default Purpose --name codex-auth-proxy Auth container name --http-name codex-http-proxy Egress container name --port, -p 18080 Internal auth data port, not host-published --admin-port 18081 Admin port published on host loopback --http-port 18082 Internal egress port, not host-published --network dock-net-proxy Shared egress network; created if missing --admin-secret Unset Server secret; configure the same value in host clients --admin-secret-file Unset Read admin authority from an owner-only 0600 file; mutually exclusive with a value --forward-default-deny true Deny general egress without destination grants --allow-model Empty (unrestricted) Repeat exact model IDs; constrained AI routes reject WebSocket --upstream-proxy Unset Explicit HTTP(S) upstream proxy, using verified destination IPs --ca-bundle Unset Additional proxy PEM roots --credential-routes Unset Owner-only 0600 broker JSON; mounted into auth only --credential-store-socket / --case-id Unset Case-specific Store connection; cannot combine with independent profiles
  • Policy flags are --forward-allow-domain, --forward-deny-domain, --forward-allow-cidr, --forward-deny-cidr, --forward-allow-port and --forward-deny-port.
  • Domain/CIDR flags repeat; port flags repeat or accept comma-separated values.

  • See policy rules (Japanese).

  • Legacy mode reads credentials as the caller's UID/GID through read-only binds under a private HOME.

  • An independent profile selected by --auth-profile NAME mounts only its directory read-write for refresh and does not load host authentication.
  • Old layouts, policy mismatches and missing worker-auth capability are rejected rather than silently updating existing containers.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
For development and custom proxy images built from source.

oaiso proxy build
oaiso proxy build --tag my-proxy:v1 -f ./docker/proxy/Dockerfile
  • --tag/-t overrides proxy_image; --dockerfile/-f selects the Dockerfile.
  • Standalone BuildKit imports OCI output into containerd.
  • Build from the repository root: the current directory is the context and Go source is required.
  • The search order is docker/proxy/Dockerfile, legacy auth-proxy.Dockerfile / docker/auth-proxy.Dockerfile, then the config directory.

docs.title: Edit network settings
docs.text:
oaiso proxy configure
  • Fields, saving and application: proxy settings UI.
  • Required order: configure, check, recreate.

docs.title: Stop and remove
docs.text:
# Both default proxies
oaiso proxy stop
oaiso proxy rm

# One named proxy
oaiso proxy stop --name codex-http-proxy
oaiso proxy rm --name codex-http-proxy
  • Use --name for custom names.
  • proxy rm --force removes a running container.
  • Finish worker tasks first; these proxies are shared services.

docs.title: Local process
docs.text:
The internal proxy serve command is available for development and standalone use:

oaiso proxy serve --role auth \
  --listen 127.0.0.1:18080 --admin-listen 127.0.0.1:18081 \
  --admin-secret-file "$HOME/.config/codex-dock/proxy-admin-secret"
  • Role auth serves AI/token/admin routes; egress forwards general traffic.
  • Create the admin-secret file first; this keeps its value out of argv.
  • The default data listen address is 0.0.0.0:18080, so set loopback explicitly for local use.
  • This command does not create Kata isolation or worker networks.

  • See standalone use.

  • Repeat oaiso proxy run --allow-model model-id to enforce exact model IDs in fixed AI request bodies.

  • See supported routes and limitations.

docs.title: oaiso run — Start a Sandbox Container
docs.text:
日本語 | English

← Command Reference

Goal Invocation Start Codex directly oaiso codex Start Claude Code directly oaiso claude Select image, worktree or mounts oaiso run --agent codex / --agent claude Authenticated shell oaiso run (built-in default) Run a command once oaiso run -- COMMAND... Item Default or setting Runtime Linux x86_64, containerd, Dragonball; --runtime kata Network Dedicated bridges, namespaces and nftables block direct access; selected proxies provide routes Default agent oaiso default codex; add --local for this project; inspect with oaiso default Images Missing images are built from the matching template or default Dockerfile Rebuilds auto_build Project settings [run] / [build] in the current repository's oaiso.toml; --project DIR selects that directory
  • Initial setup: quick start.
  • Network: network guide.
  • Custom images: build.
  • Configuration: project settings.

docs.title: Launch Codex CLI directly
docs.text:
oaiso codex
oaiso codex "Inspect this repository"
oaiso codex exec --json "Summarize the changes"
  • Arguments are forwarded verbatim to Codex.
  • The current directory is mounted at /workspace, and the worker execs Codex without an interactive shell wrapper.
  • Configure worker defaults under [run]; use oaiso run --agent codex for image, worktree, mount and detach options.
  • Starting a fresh VM takes longer than running Codex on the host.
oaiso run [OPTIONS] [IMAGE [COMMAND...]]
oaiso run [OPTIONS] -- COMMAND...  # Run in the default image
  • IMAGE and COMMAND follow Docker's positional order.
  • Put Oaiso flags before IMAGE.
  • With --image or --template, positional arguments are treated as the command.
  • The command is equivalent to --exec without quoting it as one string.
oaiso run -d --name worker codex-dock:latest
oaiso run codex-dock:latest npm test -- --watch=false
oaiso run -- npm test -- --watch=false

docs.title: Resource profiles
docs.text:
Built-in name CPU Guest memory Host reservation/limit Guest/host PID ceiling standard (default) 1 2 GiB 3 GiB 512 small 1 1 GiB 2 GiB 512 compact 1 512 MiB 768 MiB 512 
oaiso profile --node --json
oaiso run --profile-size small --agent codex
  • Bare profile shows CLI defaults; --node queries live values, including operator-defined profiles.
  • Reservations and limits are not observed memory usage; large installs/builds may exceed compact.
  • Operator PID configuration: profile define only generates JSON; it does not register a node profile.
  • Review memory measurements before choosing.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• To separate authentication from the host, use oaiso --auth-profile NAME run --proxy-admin-secret-file /private/admin-secret ... or trusted global configuration.
  • See independent profile setup.
Option Short Default Description --runtime kata Worker isolation; runc is explicit compatibility mode --kata-runtime io.containerd.kata.v2 Kata registration on dedicated containerd --image -i codex-dock:latest OCI image for the sandbox; also accepted positionally --template -T Sandbox image template (plain, pwn, etc.). Resolved to the template's image tag; an explicit --image always takes precedence. Auto-built if not present locally --pkg -p Additional packages (repeatable): apt:<pkg>, pip:<pkg>, npm:<pkg> --pkg-file Path to a package definition file (packages.dock) --project . (current dir) Directory to mount at /workspace --worktree -w false Use git worktree to isolate containers --branch -b Branch name to check out (requires --worktree) --new-branch -B false Create a new branch (requires --worktree and --branch) --name -n auto-generated Container name (defaults to codex-<adj>-<noun>) --agent shell (configurable) AI agent to launch: shell (auth-configured shell), codex, or claude --task -t Initial task prompt passed to the selected agent --exec -e Command to run once instead of the authenticated shell (details) --approval-mode suggest Agent approval mode (details) --full-auto false Deprecated: use --approval-mode full-auto --model -m Model name passed to the selected agent --read-only false Mount project directory read-only --read-only-rootfs false Make the image rootfs read-only; use tmpfs for HOME and temporary files --profile-size standard Kata VM resource profile (standard, small, or compact) --no-git-metadata false Do not automatically share linked worktree Git metadata --mount Additional host directory to mount (repeatable): <host-path>:<container-path>[:ro\|rw] (details) --no-internet false Disconnect general egress; keep fixed AI API routes --keep false Keep the container and its per-worker network after a foreground run exits (default: remove them so networks don't accumulate) --force-recreate-proxy false Recreate the Auth Proxy when its credential state differs from the host even if workers are running (existing workers lose authentication) --token-ttl 3600 Auth Proxy token TTL in seconds --agents-md Path to AGENTS.md file --detach -d false Run in background (no log output); the old -D still works --parallel -P 1 Number of parallel workers --shell -s false Start a raw (unauthenticated) shell, bypassing entrypoint.sh (debugging) --shell-type auto-detected from $SHELL, else bash Interactive shell to launch (details) --user current Container execution user (details)

docs.title: Network, isolation and startup options
docs.text:
Flag Default Purpose or limit --policy-preset Unset offline, test, dependencies, api; never widens host grants --egress-allow-domain Unset Narrow per-worker egress; repeatable --deny-read / --deny-write Empty Mask/read-only existing paths below /workspace; repeatable --watch-polling false Chokidar/Watchpack 1-second polling --ssh-proxy / --jvm-proxy false SSH CONNECT or JVM proxy settings --ca-bundle Unset Host path to additional worker PEM roots --clone-dir Unset Independent clone at a new absolute path; not with parallel launch --environment-lock Unset Validate lock and image digest --image-id Unset Require a sha256:... image digest --start-hook Empty Guest shell hook before startup; repeatable --readiness Unset Guest shell readiness probe --readiness-timeout 0 (effective 60s) Hook/probe deadline --max-lifetime / --idle-timeout / --retention 0 Lifetime, idle, exit retention; durations such as 30m or 2h; requires reap --proxy-admin-url http://127.0.0.1:18081 Host admin API --proxy-container-url http://codex-auth-proxy:18080 Worker fixed AI routes --http-proxy-url http://codex-http-proxy:18082 Worker general egress --proxy-admin-secret Unset Direct admin-secret value; prefer file-based authority --proxy-admin-secret-file Unset Owner-only 0600 admin-secret file
  • Detailed contracts: additional sandbox controls.

  • Idle tracking does not measure guest CPU or arbitrary long jobs; reap can stop a busy worker.

  • When the host and Auth Proxy credential modes differ, run automatically recreates the Auth Proxy if no workers are running.

  • If workers are running it stops with an error so their in-memory tokens are not invalidated.
  • Pass --force-recreate-proxy to recreate it anyway, then create new workers if their pinned proxy IP changed.

docs.title: Docker CLI differences
docs.text:
• run -d, run IMAGE COMMAND, ps -a, logs -f, start, stop, rm -f, and build -t use Docker style.
  • Replace the old run -d PATH project shorthand with run --project PATH.
  • The old -D still means detach.
  • In this CLI, run -p selects packages, run -i selects an image, run -t sets an agent task, and -v enables verbose output.
  • Host port publishing is not supported.
  • Use --mount HOST:CONTAINER[:ro|rw] for extra bind mounts.
  • The current project is shared at /workspace by default, and a foreground worker is removed after exit unless you pass --keep.

docs.title: --approval-mode
docs.text:
• Controls the selected agent's approval settings.
  • The selected worker runtime provides the outer isolation boundary.
Value Codex CLI flag Claude Code flag Behavior suggest (default) No approval flag No approval flag Use the agent's defaults auto-edit --ask-for-approval on-request --permission-mode acceptEdits Codex decides when to ask; Claude accepts file edits full-auto --ask-for-approval never --dangerously-skip-permissions Skip agent approval prompts danger --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --dangerously-skip-permissions Skip agent approvals and Codex's inner sandbox; preserve Kata and host restrictions
  • In a verified Kata worker, Codex's inner sandbox is set to danger-full-access to avoid nested namespace/seccomp conflicts.
  • Approval settings are separate; noninteractive exec may choose its own approval behavior.
  • Shared files remain writable according to mount permissions.
  • See security.

docs.title: --exec
docs.text:
• The configured default agent does not apply to oaiso run IMAGE COMMAND, oaiso run -- COMMAND, or --exec; these run the command.
  • An explicit --agent codex or --agent claude takes priority over the command.

  • Use --agent shell to request the authenticated shell when a different default is configured.

  • Runs a single command inside the sandbox instead of an interactive shell.

  • Passed into the container as the DOCK_EXEC_CMD environment variable, which entrypoint.sh only consults in its no-agent branch (the auth-configured shell case).

  • If --agent codex or --agent claude is given, the agent takes priority and --exec is ignored.

  • With --agent shell, the command runs.
  • Combining it with --shell (the raw debug shell that bypasses entrypoint.sh entirely) is an error, since entrypoint.sh — and therefore --exec — never runs.
  • The command runs via the shell selected by --shell-type (default bash), through its -c flag.
  • Mutually exclusive with a trailing -- command... on the command line — use whichever is more convenient; the latter avoids having to quote a multi-word command as a single string.
# Run one command in the auth-configured environment, then exit
oaiso run --exec "ls -la"

# Equivalent, without needing to quote the whole command as one string
oaiso run -- ls -la

# Run in the background
oaiso run --exec "npm test" --detach

# --agent takes priority over --exec, so this launches Codex CLI, not `ls -la`
oaiso run --agent codex --exec "ls -la"

docs.title: --shell-type
docs.text:
• Selects the shell binary used for the sandbox's interactive shell: both the auth-configured shell (when --agent is omitted) and the --shell debug mode.
  • Passed into the container as the DOCK_SHELL environment variable, which entrypoint.sh reads.
Value Behavior bash Launches bash zsh Launches zsh; requires zsh to be installed in the image
  • When neither the flag nor a config value (default_shell_type / run.shell_type) sets a value, it is auto-detected from the basename of the host's $SHELL environment variable — zsh maps to zsh, anything else (including an unset or unrecognized $SHELL) falls back to bash. This auto-detection does not apply to --shell debug mode, which always defaults to bash when the flag is omitted: --shell overrides the container's Entrypoint directly with the shell binary, bypassing entrypoint.sh entirely, so there's no way for it to fall back if that binary isn't present in the image — the engine fails to start the container.

  • Pass --shell --shell-type zsh explicitly if you want zsh there.

  • The built-in plain template includes zsh, and pwn inherits it (FROM codex-dock:latest), so --shell-type zsh works out of the box with either.

  • For a custom template, install zsh in its Dockerfile to use it.
  • Outside --shell mode (i.e. the no-agent shell and --exec), entrypoint.sh checks whether the requested shell binary actually exists before using it and logs a warning and falls back to bash if not, so a missing zsh there never fails the container outright.

The job-control wrapper that lets Ctrl+Z suspend an agent (--agent codex/claude) back to a shell prompt (launch_interactive) always uses bash internally, regardless of --shell-type — it relies on bash's PROMPT_COMMAND. --shell-type only affects the no-agent interactive shell and --shell debug mode.

# Launch the interactive shell with zsh
oaiso run --shell-type zsh

# Raw debug shell with zsh (bypasses entrypoint.sh)
oaiso run --shell --shell-type zsh

The default can be changed via default_shell_type (global) / run.shell_type (run-only) in ~/.config/codex-dock/config.toml — see the Configuration Reference.

docs.title: --user
docs.text:
Runs the container process as a specific uid:gid for filesystem permission consistency.

Value Behavior "" (omitted) Image default user (codex uid:1001) current Automatically uses the uid:gid of the user running oaiso dir Automatically uses the uid:gid of the --project directory owner uid or uid:gid Explicit value (e.g., 1000, 1000:1000)

docs.title: --mount
docs.text:
• --mount bind-mounts an arbitrary host directory into the container, in addition to /workspace (--project).
  • Repeat the flag to mount multiple directories.
--mount <host-path>:<container-path>[:ro|rw]
  • <host-path>: directory on the host (relative paths are resolved against the current working directory when oaiso run is invoked)
  • <container-path>: absolute path inside the container; /workspace is reserved for --project and cannot be used here
  • :ro / :rw: read-only / read-write (defaults to rw when omitted)
  • Mounting the same <container-path> more than once is an error
# Mount a shared dataset directory read-only
oaiso run --mount /home/user/datasets:/data:ro

# Mount multiple directories, mixing read-write and read-only
oaiso run --mount ./cache:/cache --mount /opt/models:/models:ro

Additional mounts can be independently read-only regardless of /workspace. --read-only only affects the /workspace mount.

  • --read-only-rootfs does not change /workspace or additional mount permissions.
  • Install needed packages in the image first; startup package installation is rejected.
  • HOME, /tmp, and /var/tmp are temporary tmpfs storage.

  • With --no-git-metadata, a linked worktree's shared Git metadata is not mounted; provide private metadata and mounts if Git must run inside the VM.

  • oaiso profile --json reports the CPU, guest RAM, host limit, and PID limit of each profile.

  • small provides 1 CPU, 1 GiB guest RAM, and a 2 GiB host limit; standard provides 1 CPU, 2 GiB guest RAM, and a 3 GiB host limit.
  • --profile-size small requires Kata.

  • Measure actual memory use and startup performance on the execution host.

  • This can also be set as a default via mounts in the [run] section of the config file (~/.config/codex-dock/config.toml); an explicit --mount always overrides it.

  • See doc/en/configuration.md for details.
[run]
mounts = ["/home/user/datasets:/data:ro", "./cache:/cache"]

docs.title: Package Format
docs.text:
apt:libssl-dev          # install via apt
pip:requests            # install via pip
npm:lodash              # install via npm
libssl-dev              # no prefix → treated as apt (default)

docs.title: Parallel Workers
docs.text:
oaiso run --parallel 2 --worktree --branch myfeature
  • The default node limit is 2 simultaneous workers.
  • Creates branches: myfeature-1, myfeature-2.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Basic run (mount current directory)
oaiso run

# Run with task in full-auto mode
oaiso run --agent codex --task "Write unit tests" --approval-mode full-auto

# Use git worktree on a feature branch
oaiso run --worktree --branch feature-auth --new-branch

# Run 2 parallel workers
oaiso run --parallel 2 --worktree

# Install additional packages
oaiso run --pkg "apt:libssl-dev" --pkg "pip:requests"

# Run in background
oaiso run --agent codex --task "Refactor" --approval-mode full-auto --detach

# Secure run: read-only, no internet
oaiso run --agent codex --read-only --no-internet --task "Code review"

# Use a template image (auto-built if not present)
oaiso run --image codex-dock:pwn

# Same thing via --template
oaiso run --template pwn

# Works for your own templates under ~/.config/codex-dock/templates/ too
oaiso run --template mytool

docs.title: oaiso status — consolidated readiness
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Development only; unavailable in published v0.0.2.
  • Distinguish saved credentials, checked connections and tested inference without displaying secrets.
oaiso status
oaiso status --json
Check Default behavior CLI version Show running version Selected profile Show saved state without decrypting encrypted profiles Runtime Inspect local node, Kata and builder Authentication proxy Check admin authentication, worker-token enforcement and matching profile Workers Count retained workers/sessions Updates Unchecked; no GitHub request Connection/inference Unchecked; no provider request 
[ok] version: dev
[ok] profile: work (encrypted (passphrase, age), 0600); saved, locked for this command
[unchecked] connection: Credentials were not decrypted; connection and inference not tested
...
[ok] proxy: worker-token enforcement is active; inference not tested
[ok] workers: 0 retained workers/sessions
[unchecked] updates: No external release request was made.
  • Partial example; actual status/errors include appropriate fixes.
  • locked for this command means this check has not decrypted credentials; it does not mean a running proxy was stopped.
  • Failed runtime/profile checks return exit code 1. unchecked alone is not treated as failure.

docs.title: Explicit external checks
docs.text:
oaiso status --check-connection
oaiso status --check-updates
Flag Endpoint and limits --check-connection OpenAI/Anthropic models-list endpoints using saved API keys; encrypted profiles require unlocking --check-updates Fetch GitHub's latest stable release; display it alongside the installed version
  • API checks perform no inference and do not establish inference/all-model permissions.
  • No automatic OAuth refresh or live subscription validation; check using the actual agent separately.
  • Login, encrypted storage, upgrade.

docs.title: oaiso ui — TUI Dashboard
docs.text:
日本語 | English

← Command Reference

oaiso ui

Launches a terminal UI for real-time monitoring and management of all workers.

docs.title: Key Bindings
docs.text:
Key Action on the worker list ↑ / ↓ Select worker Enter Fetch the selected worker's last 200 log lines S Stop selected worker with a 10-second grace period D Force-remove selected worker A Stop all running workers in the list R Restart a stopped worker E Fetch selected worker's proxy denial history P Open proxy settings Q Quit; from log/denial view, return to the list
  • Letter keys accept either case.
  • Stop, remove and stop-all execute without confirmation dialogs; save required artifacts first.
  • Logs and denials are fetched on opening, not followed. For live following, use logs --follow or policy events --worker WORKER --follow.
  • Authentication uses the same global settings as the CLI; configure the profile and admin secret first.

Refresh interval: Container list updates every 2 seconds.

docs.title: Proxy settings
docs.text:
oaiso proxy configure
  • Opens the editor directly, including when the node is stopped.
  • Edits global settings, or the file selected by oaiso --config PATH proxy configure.
  • Fields: allow/deny domains, CIDRs and ports; empty-grant default denial; upstream proxy URL; host CA path.
Button or key Action Validate Validate input syntax Test destination Check HOST:PORT by name/port only; no DNS or live connection Save Save settings; reject concurrent edits Reload Reload saved settings Back / Esc Return to the list, or exit the standalone editor

Successful Save output

Saved. Recreate the desired proxies/workers explicitly to apply the new settings.

  • The file has been saved. Save worker results, then recreate affected proxies and workers.

  • Does not edit API keys, real tokens or admin-secret values.

  • Saving does not update live proxies; follow network setup to recreate them.
