docs.title: oaiso update — Update oaiso itself
docs.text:
日本語 | English

← Command Reference

  • Release installations: rerun the release installer to update the CLI, node and helpers together.
  • This command updates only CLI installations managed by go install.
oaiso update

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
This installs the canonical oaiso entry point in Go's bin directory:

go install github.com/pacificbelt30/codex-dock/cmd/oaiso@latest
  • Fails with an error if go is not found on PATH.
  • For source-installed CLIs. Release installations use the release installer without adding Go.
  • oaiso is placed in $(go env GOBIN), or $(go env GOPATH)/bin when GOBIN is unset.
  • No legacy commands or aliases are generated. For existing old files, see migration (Japanese).

docs.title: Update according to installation method
docs.text:
Installation Update procedure Automatic installation or node bundle Setup update (Japanese); keep CLI, node and helpers on matching versions Manual host installation Runtime and binary update (Japanese) CLI only in Go's bin directory oaiso update; node and images require separate updates
  • Check the active path with command -v oaiso.
  • This does not update /usr/local/bin/oaiso; it installs a separate CLI in Go's bin directory.
  • make install alone does not update the node service; use the appropriate host procedure above.

docs.title: Related Documentation
docs.text: • Installation — First installation and supported hosts

docs.title: Host services and images
docs.text:
• This command does not update the node, guard, IO logger, pinned assets or proxy images.

  • See host setup and operations (Japanese).

  • Development builds also provide oaiso upgrade for distribution update plans.

docs.title: oaiso upgrade — update a binary distribution
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Development version only; unavailable in published v0.0.2. On v0.0.2, rerun the release installer.
  • No Go installation required. The command reuses the distribution installer and explains host/image update order.

docs.title: Review a plan
docs.text:
oaiso upgrade
oaiso upgrade --version v0.0.2
  • Choose one. Omit the version to query GitHub's latest stable release.
  • Download that release's install.sh and SHA256SUMS over HTTPS; run the plan only after their hashes match.
  • Checksums detect corruption or mismatched assets; they are not independent publisher signatures.
  • Planning does not replace product binaries/services. It can prepare uv/Python in user storage and download release assets.
Installed CLI: dev
Target release: v0.0.2

Host update: CLI, node, helpers and pinned runtime assets.
Images: rebuild the default worker after the host update; prepare proxies with the new CLI.
Custom images/templates: review separately.
Before applying: save work, then stop/remove retained workers and proxies with the installed CLI.
...
Plan only. Apply the same release with: oaiso upgrade --version v0.0.2 --apply
  • Example output; versions and plans depend on your host.
  • Applying v0.0.2 or earlier is refused when the selected profile root contains encrypted records. Specify another root explicitly with --auth-profile-dir; those older releases cannot read encrypted profiles.

docs.title: Apply
docs.text:
1. Review the plan and release notes.
  2. Save work; stop and remove workers/proxies using the installed CLI.
  3. Apply the reviewed version:
oaiso upgrade --version vX.Y.Z --apply
  • Replace vX.Y.Z with the reviewed release tag.
  • Run as the normal operator; the installer uses sudo for administrative changes.
  • Existing installer checks block replacement while retained/live resources or installation inconsistencies remain.
  • See setup for recovery.

docs.title: Scope and order
docs.text:
Order Target Action 1 CLI, node, guard, IO logger and pinned runtime assets Distribution installer through upgrade --apply 2 Default worker image New CLI: oaiso build --template plain --tag codex-dock:latest 3 Authentication proxy New CLI: oaiso init --agent codex or --agent claude 4 Custom images/templates Review and rebuild individually 5 Behavior Verify connections/inference in a new worker
  • Images are rebuilt with the newly installed CLI, not the old CLI still in memory.
  • oaiso update separately updates only a Go-installed CLI.

docs.title: Worker Management — ps / stop / rm / logs
docs.text:
日本語 | English

← Command Reference

docs.title: oaiso ps
docs.text:
oaiso ps [--all]

Lists running (and optionally stopped) containers.

Example oaiso ps -a output; names, elapsed times, tasks and images are illustrative:

NAME               STATUS      UPTIME  BRANCH  TASK            IMAGE
add-tests          ✅ running  5m      -       Add unit tests  codex-dock:latest
codex-calm-beacon  ⏹ exited   2m      main    (interactive)   codex-dock:latest
  • ✅ running: executing; does not establish task success.
  • ⏹ exited: finished; use ps -a, then check logs and exit status.
  • BRANCH of -: no managed worktree branch metadata.
  • UPTIME: currently elapsed time since creation; it keeps increasing after exit and does not reset on restart.
  • No workers: only column headers are displayed.

docs.title: oaiso start
docs.text:
oaiso start NAME_OR_ID
  • Restart a retained worker with the same ID and workspace.
  • Kata checks run again and the saved placeholder is restored before user code is released.
  • If a pinned proxy IP changed, create a new worker instead.
  • oaiso vm start remains available for Kata VM inventory recovery.

docs.title: oaiso exec
docs.text:
oaiso exec --json worker-name -- sh -c 'echo ok; echo warning >&2'

{"exit_code":0,"stdout":"ok\n","stderr":"warning\n"}
  • Output streams are separate. This example writes to stderr but succeeds with exit_code: 0.
  • Replace worker-name with a running worker's name.
  • The CLI returns the guest exit code; timeout is 124, cancellation is 130.

docs.title: oaiso wait
docs.text:
oaiso wait --json worker-name

For a worker whose main program exited successfully:

{"exit_code":0}
  • exit_code: 0 reports successful worker termination.
  • wait itself exits with 0 when waiting succeeds; read its output value for the worker's result.
  • Timeout is 124, cancellation is 130.

docs.title: oaiso stop
docs.text:
oaiso stop [NAME|ID...] [--all] [--timeout 10]

Stopping a container also immediately revokes its Auth Proxy token. See Token Lifecycle.

docs.title: Write a page
docs.text:
1. Start with the purpose, prerequisites and first action; link required tools to their official installation instructions.
  2. Use numbered steps and commands for procedures.
  3. Use tables for choices, settings, defaults and limitations.
  4. Keep supporting bullets short, with one point per item.

  5. Link exact flags and contracts to Reference; link detailed verification records to Development.

  6. Distinguish implemented, planned, verified and unverified behavior.

  7. Keep real credentials and tokens out of examples.
  8. Add new feature pages to both their guide category and navigation.
  9. Keep chapter classifications aligned across languages; label Japanese-only pages.
  10. Preserve existing page paths and heading links.

docs.title: Write command and output examples
docs.text:
Item Convention Copyable commands bash blocks; keep prompts such as $ and output separate Human-readable output A following text block, with success indicators and the next check JSON output json blocks; label formatting or excerpts Environment-specific values Identify example versions, IDs, PIDs, times and paths Silent success State that success produces no output and add a verification command Errors Show the failing check, recovery clue and recheck Authentication and startup Distinguish storage success, preparation, execution and task success
  • Check local output with the real CLI, an isolated HOME and fake credentials.
  • Check host-dependent output against implementation and existing evidence; adding an example does not establish live host validation.
  • For long build logs, show only useful sections and label omitted content.

docs.title: Official documentation used as references
docs.text:
Reviewed: 2026-10-22. These references inform information organization, not Oaiso's feature or platform support.

Product Organization used as a reference E2B Separate initial tutorials, examples and SDK reference Docker Sandboxes Group getting started, agents, workflows, configuration, security and CLI Daytona Group introduction, concepts, configuration, tools, security and API/CLI reference Anthropic Sandbox Runtime Installation, basic usage, overview and how it works Claude Code sandbox Separate setup, configuration, mechanism, troubleshooting and limitations

docs.title: Validate
docs.text:
• Requires uv. Use managed Python 3.12, as in host setup and CI.
  • Run from the repository root.
uv python install 3.12
uv run --no-project --no-config --managed-python --python 3.12 --with-requirements requirements-docs.txt mkdocs build --strict
  • Check navigation coverage, page links and heading links.
  • Compare commands with the implementation; distinguish syntax checks from live host validation.
  • Compare command/flag tables with normal subcommand --help; native codex/claude help is forwarded to the agent.
  • Compare allowed keys, types, scope and precedence in both languages, including different global/project hook formats.
  • Walk authentication and update procedures from prerequisites through settings, preparation and verification; link checks alone do not establish runtime correctness.

docs.title: Local encrypted credential store specification
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Development specification; unavailable in published v0.0.2.
  • Usage, Store contract.

docs.title: Defaults and dependencies
docs.text:
Item Contract Default New login profiles use Secret Service; existing profiles and low-level set/import remain unchanged; explicit --encrypt/--plaintext alternatives Location Private product profiles on the control host, outside workspace/clone/additional shares Encrypted data API keys, OAuth access/refresh/ID tokens, credential versions and connection generations Implementation Embed filippo.io/age v1.3.2 in the Go binary External dependencies Passphrase mode needs no network, external age CLI, additional daemon or database Proxy admin authority Separate 0600 file; outside this store and never shared with work VMs Go Minimum 1.26.0; development/CI toolchain 1.27.3. Binary-distribution users need no Go
  • Official age source, format specification, Go API.

docs.title: Format and cryptography
docs.text:
Element Contract File NAME/NAME.vault, a single atomically updated JSON manifest Manifest version Oaiso schema 2, separate from the standard age format version Public metadata Profile name, unlock backend, key ID, public age recipient and protected key file Credential ciphertext Standard binary age stream, base64 encoded in the manifest, encrypted to an X25519 recipient Secret bundle Product-specific age private identity plus an independent random 32-byte authentication key Store authentication HMAC-SHA256 binds the manifest and credential ciphertext Complete reads Consume the age stream through EOF, validating the final chunk and size limit before use
  • Public-key age encryption does not authenticate the sender. The separate authentication key prevents someone knowing only the recipient from replacing stored credentials undetected; protect it together with the private identity.
  • age implements credential/key-bundle encryption. No custom cipher, age recipient or age-format parser is implemented.
  • The whole .vault file is a JSON manifest, not direct input to the age CLI. Interoperability tests extract its age ciphertext and decrypt it with the official CLI.
  • Keeping one file avoids multi-file transactions during ordinary OAuth refresh.

docs.title: Key protection
docs.text:
Method Contract Passphrase Encrypt the secret bundle using an age scrypt recipient; hidden TTY or dedicated FD New scrypt cost logN=17, r=8, p=1, approximately 128 MiB workspace; explicit small-control-host budget Accepted maximum SetMaxWorkFactor(18) prevents unbounded file-supplied KDF work Input limits New passphrases 12–4096 bytes; explicit descriptor >= 3, maximum 4096 bytes Keyring New-login default; store/read-back the bundle through an existing service or an explicit private session Keyring requirements Host secret-tool and user D-Bus; 15-second operation timeout Everyday use Unlock on proxy startup; no repeated prompt while the same proxy is running Refresh cost Reuse the unlocked identity and encrypt to its public recipient; no scrypt per inference/refresh
  • age CLI defaults to logN=18; Oaiso explicitly uses 17 for its 128 MiB budget and accepts reads up to 18. Implementation.
  • No automatic unlocking through a plaintext key alongside ciphertext.
  • OS keyring encryption/locking depend on OS configuration. Unavailable backends never switch to passphrases, plaintext or host credentials.
  • No direct backend-conversion command; reauthenticate into a new profile using the other backend.

docs.title: Proxy and VM boundary
docs.text:
1. Unlock the identity/authentication-key bundle in host CLI memory.
  2. Transfer it to the existing Auth Proxy through a bounded, length-prefixed private stdin stream.
  3. Drop the long-running host command's unlocked references after proxy readiness.
  4. Give work VMs only short-lived, proxy-scoped placeholders.
Boundary Contract argv/environment/configuration/container metadata/ordinary logs No secret bundle or real credentials Stdin protocol Maximum 1024 bytes; reject partial input, disconnect and excessive lengths Proxy reuse Match profile, protected-key fingerprint, connection generation and protocol Older proxy protocol Drain workers and explicitly remove/recreate the authentication proxy Work VMs No ciphertext, identity, authentication key, credential socket or control-host HOME Login-only Kata Separate temporary memory-only collection using the pinned official CLI

docs.title: Persistence and locking
docs.text:
Operation Contract OAuth refresh Cross-process lock and atomic expected-version CAS; retain connection generation Durable save Ciphertext temporary file, fsync, atomic rename and directory fsync Failure/conflict Never acknowledge success; propagate to existing proxy revocation behavior Product lock Stop workers/proxies belonging to this private store; retain work/ciphertext OS keyring lock Does not erase an already-unlocked proxy; run auth profile lock separately Process close Clear owned key/authentication-key byte slices and drop the age identity reference
  • Public credentialstore.Store is unchanged.
  • Go cannot guarantee zeroing every temporary secret copy; bound lifetime, including process termination.

docs.title: Explicit migration
docs.text:
Source Operation Plaintext .json auth profile encrypt NAME; verify age persistence/read-back before deleting plaintext Encrypted schema 1 auth profile migrate-age NAME; unlock using its original backend and explicitly convert Ordinary schema-1 writes/new proxy startup Refuse; no automatic conversion or credential fallback Migration generation Rotate credential/connection versions; old workers cannot be reauthorized Recovery backup Retain NAME.vault.v1-backup with mode 0600; ciphertext only, never loaded automatically Conflicting backup Refuse overwrite; preserve recovery data Retry/interruption Validate using the selected backend and resume; an already-migrated profile does not rotate again Coexisting plaintext/ciphertext Fail closed until explicit migration compares content and completes Passphrase change Reprotect the same identity/authentication key; retain connection generation
  • Argon2id/XChaCha20-Poly1305 remain only in the read-only schema-1 decoder, never new writes.
  • Keyring migration retains the old keyring item for encrypted-backup recovery; operators can remove retired backups/items after verification.
  • Backups still decrypt with old passphrases/keys. Deleted blocks and earlier backups are not securely erased.

docs.title: Protection and verification
docs.text:
• Primary target: reading inactive credential files, disks and backups.
  • Outside this protection: control-host root/same-UID process access, live memory, swap and outer VM snapshots.
  • Local-only storage cannot fully detect a snapshot rolling back keys, ciphertext and generation state together.
  • WSL uses private Linux storage; reject unverified DrvFS/NFS/FUSE filesystems.
  • Results, measurements and remaining checks.

docs.title: Keyring sessions
docs.text:
• User guide: existing desktop service discovery and private headless sessions.
  • The CLI owns foreground D-Bus and GNOME Keyring processes; normal exit, SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP cancel and reap them.
  • Keys stay in the separate private keyring files and proxy memory; no passphrase file or global PAM modification.
  • Share validation rejects keyring storage and filesystem D-Bus socket paths.

docs.title: Prepare development tools
docs.text:
日本語 | English

Purpose Go, Make and Git Install a prebuilt release Not required; the installer also prepares missing uv/Python Build the CLI, node and helpers from source Required; follow this page Build a product embedding the Go API Go is required in the build environment, which can be separate from the execution host

docs.title: Required tools and official instructions
docs.text:
Tool Purpose or requirement Official instructions or downloads Go go.mod requires at least 1.26.0; builds the CLI, node and helpers Linux installation, downloads and SHA-256 GNU Make Build and test targets Official downloads and documentation Git Source checkout and version control Linux installation curl Download release assets Official download guide uv Isolated host Python and dependency management Installation Python 3.12 Setup, validation and documentation scripts Install Python with uv C compiler Go race tests; also builds the static PID hook during manual Kata preparation GCC installation
  • Python uses uv-managed distributions, rather than a source build of Python itself.
  • The commands below target Ubuntu 26.04 on Linux x86_64. Go uses the official archive; Git, Make and GCC use Ubuntu packages.

docs.title: 1. Prepare basic tools
docs.text:
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y curl ca-certificates git make build-essential

docs.title: 2. Install Go using the official Linux procedure
docs.text:
Skip to step 3 if a suitable Go installation is already available.

  1. Check the stable Linux amd64 archive and SHA-256 on the official download page, then download and verify it.

    curl -fL -o go1.27.3.linux-amd64.tar.gz https://go.dev/dl/go1.27.3.linux-amd64.tar.gz
echo '65efbc80fdc1fa2cd2631cad5b481777a68e8725f34e89f50fc6ac714e379b40  go1.27.3.linux-amd64.tar.gz' | sha256sum --check -
    • 1.27.3 is an example. For another version, change the filename, URL and SHA-256 together.
    • Expected: go1.27.3.linux-amd64.tar.gz: OK. Do not continue if verification fails.

  2. After successful verification, remove the existing /usr/local/go tree and extract the archive as instructed by Go.

    sudo rm -rf /usr/local/go
sudo tar -C /usr/local -xzf go1.27.3.linux-amd64.tar.gz
    • This replaces the toolchain under /usr/local/go. Do not extract over an existing Go tree.

  3. Add the following line to ~/.profile and also run it in the current shell.

    export PATH="/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH"

  4. Verify the active installation.

    command -v go
go version

    /usr/local/go/bin/go
go version go1.27.3 linux/amd64
    • The version should match the installed archive. If another Go is selected, check PATH ordering.

docs.title: 3. Prepare uv and Python
docs.text:
Only install uv if it is missing, using its official versioned installer.

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/0.13.5/install.sh | sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
uv python install 3.12
uv --version
uv python find --no-project --no-config --managed-python --system 3.12
  • uv 0.13.5 matches CI. If uv is already installed, only prepare and check Python.
  • The last command should print the absolute path of a uv-managed Python 3.12 executable.
  • The OS Python is retained.

docs.title: 4. Continue to build or validate
docs.text:
• Build and deploy from source (Japanese)
  • Code validation (Japanese)
  • Documentation editing

  • Create a release (Japanese)

  • The selected age and patched HTTP/2 dependencies require Go 1.26.0 or later. Development/CI use toolchain go1.27.3 from go.mod. Binary-distribution users do not need Go.

Goal Codex Claude Code Forward native CLI arguments oaiso codex oaiso claude Set image, worktree or mount options oaiso run --agent codex oaiso run --agent claude Set the default for oaiso run oaiso default codex oaiso default claude

docs.text: Item Behavior Real credentials Stay in the host Auth Proxy; never passed to work VMs Worker AI traffic Short-lived placeholders authorize fixed AI routes General traffic Denied by default; allow required destinations (Japanese) CLI model selection Selects a model; authorization also requires proxy model limits Agent approvals Configured with the run options; separate from Kata isolation

docs.title: Authentication and profiles
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Prerequisite: complete installation.
  • Configure authentication on the trusted host, including a WSL or VM host.

docs.title: 1. Choose credential separation
docs.text:
Mode Credential storage Use it for Independent profile (recommended for separation) Product directory with mode 0700; files with mode 0600 Separate product authentication from host CLI logins Legacy host integration Host credential files and authentication environment variables Reuse existing host authentication Embedding product Store Storage provided by the embedding application Manage per-case credentials through the Go API
  • Selected independent profiles never fall back to host authentication.
  • The manual set/import examples below use 0600 plaintext. New development login profiles default to keyring plus age.
  • Keep credentials and profile selection out of project oaiso.toml files.

docs.title: 2. Choose the agent and authentication method
docs.text:
Agent API key Subscription Codex CLI Register an OpenAI key Import Codex OAuth credentials Claude Code Register an Anthropic key Import Claude OAuth credentials; see Claude setup-token

For an independent profile, run exactly one command below. All alternatives use the name work.

Authentication Command OpenAI API key oaiso auth profile set work --provider openai Anthropic API key oaiso auth profile set work --provider anthropic Codex OAuth oaiso auth profile import work --format codex --credentials-stdin < /private/login/auth.json Claude OAuth oaiso auth profile import work --format claude --credentials-stdin < /private/login/.credentials.json

Successful registration output

Operation Output Register API key Profile created (plaintext, 0600). Import OAuth Profile imported (plaintext, 0600).
  • API-key entry shows API key:; typed characters are hidden.

  • This confirms storage, not key validity or subscription access.

  • Replace /private/login/... with the actual JSON path from a prior official CLI login.

  • OAuth import separates the copied credentials from the host CLI's storage; later logins are not automatically synchronized.
  • auth profile set: hidden TTY input; keep real keys out of command arguments.
  • auth profile import: explicit stdin input; source files are not automatically discovered or deleted.
  • Legacy host integration: prepare credentials.

docs.title: 3. Configure admin authority and profile selection
docs.text:
1. Create the admin secret in a separate 0600 file.
  2. Select the profile globally.
  3. Set auth_profile to the created name, work. Replace /home/user/... with your actual absolute path.
  4. Check the selected authentication mode:
oaiso auth show

Output for a selected OpenAI API-key profile

Profile: work
Storage: plaintext (0600)
OpenAI: api-key
Anthropic: disabled
Registered credentials Expected line OpenAI API key OpenAI: api-key Codex OAuth OpenAI: oauth Anthropic API key Anthropic: api-key Claude OAuth Anthropic: oauth Provider without credentials disabled; cannot launch that provider
  • Expected in profile mode: Profile: work, and api-key or oauth for the selected provider.
  • Creating a profile does not select it. Before selection, auth show reports legacy OpenAI information.
  • Published v0.0.2 uses the manual registration/import above. The development version also offers login Kata and live API connection checks.

docs.title: 4. Continue to the first worker
docs.text:
1. If needed, allow general network destinations.
  2. Return to image and proxy preparation.

  3. Prepare Codex for an OpenAI profile, or Claude for an Anthropic profile.

  4. init checks for a credential source; the first live agent request separately checks provider authentication.

docs.title: Refresh and switching
docs.text:
Operation Behavior Normal OAuth refresh CAS save to the same Store; retain the connection generation Re-login or account switch Import into a new profile, then replace the workers and proxy Credentials passed to workers Short-lived placeholders only; no real API key or access/refresh/ID token Login Kata, automated login and API connection checks Implemented in development; live-account verification remains separate Encrypted vault and key backends Not implemented; see design requirements
  • Storage, permissions and limitations: Security.
  • Flags and file paths: Authentication command reference.

docs.title: Encrypt stored credentials
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Development only; unavailable in published v0.0.2.
  • New login profiles use the keyring by default. Existing profiles and low-level auth profile set/import keep their existing behavior.
  • Supports API keys and subscription credentials. The Auth Proxy remains; work VMs receive no real credentials.

docs.title: Choose a backend
docs.text:
Backend Use case Requirements Passphrase WSL, Linux VMs, SSH and headless hosts A long passphrase, at least 12 bytes Keyring (new-login default) Desktop, SSH, WSL and VMs Secret Service, user D-Bus, secret-tool; setup and headless use
  • age is embedded: no additional age executable, service, database, Vault or container; storage/unlocking are local.
  • Use an existing desktop service or an explicitly opened private session; failure never switches backends. Keyring storage protection depends on its OS configuration.
  • Existing keyring unlock dialogs may appear. Unanswered operations fail after 15 seconds.
  • secret-tool manual; Ubuntu packages it as libsecret-tools.

docs.title: Create an encrypted login
docs.text:
oaiso login --agent codex --method subscription --profile work --encrypt
  • Enter and confirm a hidden passphrase.
  • Choose --method api-key for an API key; --agent claude for Claude Code.
  • Subscription login runs in temporary Kata; collected credentials are encrypted directly.
  • Existing profiles are never overwritten; choose a different name.

Use --keyring instead of --encrypt for an existing OS keyring:

oaiso login --agent claude --method api-key --profile claude-work --keyring

docs.title: Start, inspect and lock
docs.text:
oaiso init --agent codex
oaiso status
oaiso auth profile show work
oaiso auth profile lock work
Action Behavior Proxy startup/restart Unlock on host; transfer the data key through container stdin Additional tasks with a running proxy Check wrapped-key fingerprint and connection generation; reuse without another prompt status, profile show/list Show storage metadata without decryption status --check-connection Explicitly unlock and check API keys through models APIs; no inference profile lock Stop affected workers and authentication proxies; retain work and ciphertext
  • show reporting locked means that command has not decrypted credentials. Inspect the separate status proxy check for a running proxy.
  • Lock interrupts work; save results first.
  • Stopping the proxy or rebooting also discards its process-local key.
  • OS keyring locking does not erase an already-unlocked proxy key; use profile lock separately. That command does not lock the OS keyring itself.
  • Old proxy images need rebuilding; drain workers before recreating proxies.

docs.title: Migrate plaintext
docs.text:
1. Save work and stop affected workers.
  2. Stop the authentication proxy.
  3. Explicitly migrate:
oaiso auth profile encrypt work
  • Save ciphertext, read it back and verify before removing work.json.
  • Migration rotates connection generation; create new workers instead of reauthorizing old ones.
  • If interrupted with both records present, normal reads fail closed. Repeat the same command/passphrase to compare credentials and complete migration.
  • Different content is never silently removed.
  • Deleted disk blocks and old backups are not securely erased.

docs.title: Migrate the older encrypted format
docs.text:
oaiso auth profile show work
oaiso auth profile lock work
oaiso auth profile migrate-age work
oaiso init --agent codex
  • Format: legacy-v1 identifies the old format; new records show Format: age.
  • Save work first. Stop/remove old proxies, then migrate using the original passphrase or keyring.
  • Verify age persistence/read-back and rotate connection generation; create new workers.
  • Retain work.vault.v1-backup as 0600 ciphertext, never automatically loaded.
  • Retry the same command after interruption; a different backup is never overwritten.
  • Retrying an already migrated record verifies it without rotating generations again.
  • Keyring migration also retains the old keyring item for backup recovery; operators can remove retired items after verification.
  • New proxy startup/refresh on the old format is refused, without plaintext/host credential fallback.
  • Host setup --rollback does not downgrade credential formats. Prefer reauthentication when recovering an older version; do not resume old workers.

docs.title: Change a passphrase
docs.text:
oaiso auth profile lock work
oaiso auth profile passwd work
  • Unlock with the old passphrase, then enter/confirm the new one.
  • Remove stopped profile proxies, then protect the same age private identity/authentication key using the new passphrase.
  • Refuse changes while profile workers/proxies are running; unavailable for keyring-backed profiles.
  • Run oaiso init with the new passphrase to restart the proxy.

docs.title: Noninteractive unlocking
docs.text:
oaiso --passphrase-fd 3 init --agent codex 3< /private/runtime/passphrase-input
  • This demonstrates FD wiring. Supply a private secret source or temporary pipe, never a passphrase file in the project or alongside ciphertext.
  • Descriptor >= 3, maximum 4096 bytes, one trailing newline removed. Separate it from API-key stdin.
  • No passphrase arguments/environment variables.
  • For passwd, provide old input using --passphrase-fd and separate new input using --new-passphrase-fd.

docs.title: Format and limits
docs.text:
Item Specification Storage ~/.config/codex-dock/profiles/NAME/NAME.vault; 0700 directories, 0600 files Container JSON manifest containing standard age ciphertext/protected-key data; the whole .vault is not direct age CLI input Cipher age v1.3.2 X25519 recipient; HMAC-SHA256 also prevents public-key-only substitution Key protection age scrypt, logN=17 (approximately 128 MiB), only when unlocking OS keyring age private identity/authentication-key bundle in existing Secret Service Secret location Unlocked host command/proxy memory; only placeholders in work VMs Main protection Reading inactive files, disks and backups Outside protection Host root/same-UID process access, live memory, swap and outer VM snapshots
  • WSL uses private Linux storage. Reject unverified DrvFS/NFS/FUSE filesystems. Kata separately requires KVM.
  • Lost passphrases/keyring keys cannot be recovered; reauthenticate into a new profile.
  • Local-only storage cannot fully detect rollback of a VM snapshot containing both keys and ciphertext.
  • Detailed specification, verification and remaining gaps.

docs.title: Manage credential keys with a keyring
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • Development only; unavailable in published v0.0.2.
  • New oaiso login profiles use Secret Service by default. Existing profiles keep their storage backend.
  • API keys and OAuth tokens remain age-encrypted in .vault. The keyring holds the age private identity and authentication key.
  • Work VMs receive no keyring, D-Bus socket or real credentials.

docs.title: Choose a session
docs.text:
Environment Action Available desktop keyring Run oaiso login normally; an unlocked keyring needs no additional input SSH, WSL or headless VM Open oaiso auth keyring session Without a keyring Choose login --encrypt for a product passphrase Explicit plaintext Choose login --plaintext; 0700 directories and 0600 files
  • No GUI, TPM or USB key is required.
  • An unavailable keyring fails closed. A disposable store/read/delete probe runs before provider login or API-key collection.

docs.title: 1. Install dependencies
docs.text:
Development oaiso setup installs missing D-Bus, GNOME Keyring and secret-tool dependencies. Offline setup requires these packages in advance. Manual Ubuntu installation:

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install --no-install-recommends dbus-daemon gnome-keyring libsecret-tools
Component Purpose and official documentation D-Bus User-process communication; official session runner GNOME Keyring Key storage/unlocking; project, daemon manual secret-tool Secret Service store/lookup/delete; official implementation

The full GNOME desktop is unnecessary; distribution packages can still pull GUI-related libraries.

docs.title: 2. Desktop use
docs.text:
oaiso auth keyring check
oaiso login --agent codex --method subscription --profile work
oaiso init --agent codex

Keyring: ready (store/read/delete verified; no provider request).
  • check uses a random disposable item; existing secrets are never displayed.
  • Without DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, Oaiso discovers the owned bus socket in the user's private 0700 runtime directory.
  • An existing PAM configuration may unlock the keyring at OS login. Oaiso never receives the OS password.
  • Oaiso does not edit PAM. Passwordless logins, including SSH public-key authentication, may need a separate unlock. PAM documentation.

docs.title: 3. Headless use
docs.text:
oaiso auth keyring session
  1. Enter and confirm a private passphrase on first use; enter it once subsequently.
  2. Oaiso starts private D-Bus and GNOME Keyring processes and unlocks storage.
  3. Use ordinary commands inside the opened shell:
oaiso auth keyring check
oaiso login --agent claude --method api-key --profile claude-work
oaiso init --agent claude
oaiso claude
exit
  • The 12–4096-byte passphrase is independent of the OS login password.
  • Encrypted storage lives at ~/.config/codex-dock/keyring/keyrings/, separate from the desktop keyring.
  • CLI processes in the session share the unlocked service.
  • Exiting stops the private keyring and D-Bus; encrypted storage remains.
  • Concurrent private sessions using the same storage are rejected.
  • An already-running Auth Proxy retains its own in-memory key. Run oaiso auth profile lock NAME before leaving if the proxy must also lock.
  • Later unlocking of these profiles must also run inside keyring session.

To run one command:

oaiso auth keyring session -- oaiso auth keyring check

Explicit noninteractive input uses global --passphrase-fd. Never store the passphrase in argv, environment or a plaintext file.

docs.title: Existing profiles
docs.text:
• Existing plaintext/passphrase profiles remain usable.
  • To change backend, log in to a new profile name with the intended keyring available.
  • No automatic keyring copying or conversion of existing passphrase profiles.
  • age format and profile locking, verification and limitations.

docs.title: Allow general network traffic
docs.text:
日本語 | English

Traffic Default Fixed Codex/Claude AI routes Authorized by live placeholders, provider and model rules Git, npm, pip and arbitrary websites General egress; disconnected without a domain or CIDR grant Direct VM traffic, host and other workers Blocked

docs.title: 1. Configure host destination grants
docs.text:
• File: ~/.config/codex-dock/config.toml.
  • This example grants GitHub and npm. Add actual distribution and redirect destinations as needed.
  • Merge into the existing [proxy] table; retain admin_secret_file and other keys.
[proxy]
forward_default_deny = true
forward_allow_domains = ["github.com", "registry.npmjs.org"]
forward_allow_ports = [80, 443]
Setting Meaning github.com Domain and subdomains =api.github.com Exact hostname only Ports alone Do not grant destinations Domain and CIDR allowlists together Both must match; denials always win Private, loopback and metadata IPs Cannot be unblocked with a CIDR grant
  • GitHub asset downloads may use other domains not granted by this example.
  • SSH, JVM and custom CA behavior: compatibility settings.

docs.title: 2. Check before launch
docs.text:
oaiso policy check --json
oaiso policy explain registry.npmjs.org:443 --json

Output of the second command with the grants above

{
  "destination": {"Host": "registry.npmjs.org", "Port": 443},
  "allowed": true,
  "code": "address_not_checked",
  "stage": "destination",
  "addresses_checked": 0,
  "complete": false
}
  • Formatted for readability; the CLI emits one line.
  • allowed: true, complete: false: hostname and port passed; DNS IP checks have not run. This does not prove live connectivity.
  • A valid policy check returns exit code 0 and policy JSON with source: configuration for NEW workers; not a live update.

Also check a destination without a grant

oaiso policy explain example.com:443 --json

{
  "destination": {"Host": "example.com", "Port": 443},
  "allowed": false,
  "code": "domain_not_allowed",
  "stage": "destination",
  "addresses_checked": 0,
  "complete": true
}
  • Denial is expected here. explain itself succeeds; inspect allowed and code rather than the command's exit status for the policy decision.

  • Without destination grants: code: general_egress_disabled. Fixed AI routes are separate.

  • These inspect host settings for new workers; they do not change live traffic.

  • explain opens no connection; this example checks hostname and port only.
  • Add --resolve to check DNS result IPs; this still does not test live service connectivity.
  • Interactive editing: oaiso proxy configure, also available when the node is stopped.

docs.title: 3. Apply to new workers
docs.text:
Current state Action First setup Continue to init in the quick start Existing proxies/workers Save results, stop/remove workers, stop/remove affected proxies, run init with the new settings, create new workers
  • Saving settings does not update existing proxies, CONNECT tunnels or workers.
  • Procedure and names: proxy recreation (Japanese).
  • Per-worker --egress-allow-domain and presets narrow host grants; they cannot add destinations denied by the host.

docs.title: 4. Inspect or stop a worker
docs.text:
oaiso policy show --worker WORKER --json
oaiso policy events --worker WORKER --json
  • Replace WORKER with a name from oaiso ps -a.
  • Denial history is shared by workers on the same egress proxy; it is not an independent per-run audit log.
  • Immediate cutoff: oaiso policy quarantine --worker WORKER. Stops communication and all jobs, and forbids restarting that worker.
  • Retention, artifacts and failure handling: quarantine contract.
  • Detailed rules: network policy (Japanese).

docs.title: 認証と通信を設定する
docs.text: やりたいこと ガイド ホストと製品の認証を分ける 認証方式とプロファイル 通信先を許可・拒否する 設定手順・判定規則 資格情報の保持先・隔離の限界を確認する セキュリティ 認証Proxyの仕組みを確認する 認証プロキシ Proxyを別の構成で使う プロキシの単体利用

docs.title: 次に調べる
docs.text:
• フラグ・設定・APIの正確な仕様：リファレンス。
  • ホスト更新・障害対応：管理・運用。
  • アプリケーションへの組み込み：Go API。

docs.title: エージェント
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • 前提：実行ホスト・認証・ワーカーイメージの準備。
  • 作業場所：エージェントに扱わせるプロジェクトのディレクトリ。

docs.title: 対応状況
docs.text: エージェント APIキー サブスク 詳細 Codex CLI OpenAI APIキー ChatGPT OAuth 認証の準備・起動オプション Claude Code Anthropic APIキー Claude OAuth／setup-token Claude Code その他 未対応 未対応 今後の対応

docs.title: 起動方法を選ぶ
docs.text:
目的 Codex Claude Code 公式CLIの引数をそのまま渡す oaiso codex oaiso claude image・worktree・mountなどを指定する oaiso run --agent codex oaiso run --agent claude oaiso run の既定にする oaiso default codex oaiso default claude
  • oaiso codex / oaiso claude の引数：エージェントCLIへ渡す。
  • Oaisoの起動フラグ：oaiso run --agent ... へ指定。
  • 直接起動時の独立プロファイル：信頼済みグローバル設定で選択。
  • oaiso run の組み込み既定値：認証済みシェル。
  • プロジェクトだけの既定変更：oaiso default codex --local など。

docs.title: 認証・通信・承認の境界
docs.text: 項目 扱い 実資格情報 ホスト側Auth Proxyで保持。作業VMへ渡さない ワーカーのAI通信 短命トークンで固定AI経路を利用 一般通信 既定拒否。必要な宛先を許可 モデル名の指定 CLIのモデル選択。モデル認可はProxy側の制限も必要 エージェントの承認 承認モードで指定。Kataの隔離と別の設定

docs.title: 次の操作
docs.text:
• ファイル共有・worktree。
  • ワーカーの一覧・ログ・停止・再起動。
  • CLI・イメージの更新。
  • Go APIでのエージェント実行。

docs.title: 認証方式とプロファイル
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • 前提：インストールを完了。
  • 設定場所：信頼済みホスト側。WSL／VMをホストにする場合も同様。

docs.location: guides/authentication/#1-認証の分離方法を選ぶ
docs.title: 1. 認証の分離方法を選ぶ
docs.text:
方式 資格情報の保持先 選ぶ場合 独立プロファイル（ホストと分ける場合の推奨） 製品専用の0700ディレクトリ・0600ファイル ホストCLIのログインと製品の認証を分ける 従来のホスト連携 ホストの認証ファイル・認証環境変数 既存のホスト認証を利用する 組み込み製品のStore 組み込み側が提供する保存先 ケースごとの認証をGo APIで管理する
  • 独立プロファイル選択時：ホスト認証へfallbackしない。
  • 以下の手動set/import例は0600平文保存。開発版の新規loginはキーリング＋ageが既定です。
  • プロジェクトの oaiso.toml：資格情報・認証プロファイル設定を置かない。

docs.location: guides/authentication/#2-エージェントと認証方式を選ぶ
docs.title: 2. エージェントと認証方式を選ぶ
docs.text:
エージェント APIキー サブスク Codex CLI OpenAI APIキーを登録 Codex形式のOAuthをimport Claude Code Anthropic APIキーを登録 Claude形式のOAuthをimport。setup-tokenはClaudeの手順

独立プロファイルは、以下から1つだけ実行。例では名前を work に統一します。

認証 実行するコマンド OpenAI APIキー oaiso auth profile set work --provider openai Anthropic APIキー oaiso auth profile set work --provider anthropic Codex OAuth oaiso auth profile import work --format codex --credentials-stdin < /private/login/auth.json Claude OAuth oaiso auth profile import work --format claude --credentials-stdin < /private/login/.credentials.json

登録成功時の出力

操作 表示 APIキー登録 Profile created (plaintext, 0600). OAuth import Profile imported (plaintext, 0600).
  • APIキー入力時：API key: と表示。入力内容は画面に出ない。

  • この表示は保存成功。キーの有効性やサブスク利用可否の検証結果ではない。

  • /private/login/...：事前に公式CLIで認証したJSONの実際のパスへ置換。

  • OAuth import：コピー時点でホストCLIの保存先と分離。その後のログイン変更は自動同期しない。
  • auth profile set：TTYから非表示入力。引数へ実キーを書かない。
  • auth profile import：明示したstdinから入力。元ファイルは自動探索・削除しない。
  • 従来のホスト連携：認証ソースの準備。

docs.location: guides/authentication/#3-管理シークレットとプロファイルを設定する
docs.title: 3. 管理シークレットとプロファイルを設定する
docs.text:
1. 管理シークレットを作成。資格情報とは別の0600ファイルに保存。
  2. グローバル設定でプロファイルを選択。
  3. 設定の auth_profile は、上で作成した work に合わせる。/home/user/... は実際の絶対パスへ置換。
  4. 認証方式を確認。
oaiso auth show

OpenAI APIキーを選択した場合の出力

Profile: work
Storage: plaintext (0600)
OpenAI: api-key
Anthropic: disabled
登録した認証 確認する行 OpenAI APIキー OpenAI: api-key Codex OAuth OpenAI: oauth Anthropic APIキー Anthropic: api-key Claude OAuth Anthropic: oauth 未登録のprovider disabled。そのproviderでの起動はできない
  • 独立プロファイルの期待値：Profile: work と、選択したproviderの api-key または oauth。
  • プロファイルを作成しただけでは選択されない。設定前の auth show は従来モードのOpenAI情報を表示。
  • 公開済みv0.0.2は上記の手動登録・importを使用。開発版は専用KataログインとAPI接続確認にも対応。

docs.title: 4. 初回起動へ進む
docs.text:
1. 必要なら一般通信の宛先を設定。
  2. クイックスタートのイメージ・Proxy準備へ戻る。

  3. work にOpenAIを登録した場合はCodex、Anthropicを登録した場合はClaudeを準備・起動。

  4. init は認証ソースの存在を確認する。実サービスでの認証成功は、エージェントの最初の要求で別途確認。

docs.title: 更新と切り替え
docs.text:
操作 扱い 通常のOAuth更新 同じStoreへCAS保存。接続世代を維持 再ログイン・別アカウントへの切り替え 新規プロファイルへ取り込み、ワーカーとProxyを切り替える ワーカーへ渡す資格情報 短命トークンのみ。実APIキー・access/refresh/ID tokenは返さない 認証専用Kata・自動login・API接続確認 開発版で実装。実アカウントでの確認は別途必要 暗号化Vault・鍵backend 未実装。設計要件
  • 保持先・権限・制限：セキュリティ。
  • フラグと保存先：認証コマンドリファレンス。

docs.title: 認証情報を暗号化して保存する
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • 開発版の機能です。公開済みv0.0.2には含まれません。
  • 新規loginはキーリング方式が既定。既存プロファイルと低水準のauth profile set/importは従来の方式を維持します。
  • APIキー・サブスクの両方が対象です。認証Proxyを維持し、作業VMへ実資格情報を渡しません。

docs.title: 方式を選ぶ
docs.text:
方式 選ぶ場面 必要なもの パスフレーズ WSL・Linux VM・SSH・GUIなし 12バイト以上の長いパスフレーズ キーリング（新規loginの既定） デスクトップ・SSH・WSL・VM Secret Service、利用者D-Bus、secret-tool。準備とGUIなしの使い方
  • ageをバイナリへ組み込むため、追加のageコマンド・サービス・DB・Vault・コンテナは不要です。ローカルで保存・解錠できます。
  • 既存のデスクトップサービス、または明示的な専用セッションを使い、利用不能ならエラーにします。OSキーリング側の保存時の保護は、その設定に依存します。
  • OSキーリングのロック解除は、既存サービスの画面が開く場合があります。応答できない場合は15秒で失敗します。
  • secret-tool：公式マニュアル。Ubuntuではlibsecret-toolsに含まれます。

docs.location: guides/encrypted-credentials/#暗号化してログインする
docs.title: 暗号化してログインする
docs.text:
oaiso login --agent codex --method subscription --profile work --encrypt
  • パスフレーズを非表示で2回入力。
  • APIキーなら--method api-key、Claude Codeなら--agent claudeを選択。
  • サブスク認証は一時Kataで実施し、回収した認証情報を直接暗号化して保存。
  • 既存プロファイルは上書きしません。別名を指定してください。

OSキーリングを使う場合は--encryptの代わりに--keyringを指定します。

oaiso login --agent claude --method api-key --profile claude-work --keyring

docs.title: 起動・確認・ロック
docs.text:
oaiso init --agent codex
oaiso status
oaiso auth profile show work
oaiso auth profile lock work
操作 動作 Proxyの初回起動・再起動 ホストで解錠し、既存Proxyへ鍵を標準入力で渡す Proxy稼働中の追加タスク 同じ暗号化ヘッダーと接続世代を確認して再利用。再入力不要 status・profile show/list 復号せず、保存方式と未確認の状態を表示 status --check-connection 明示的に解錠してAPIキーをモデル一覧APIで確認。推論は行わない profile lock 対象ワーカーと認証Proxyを停止。成果物と暗号文は保持
  • showのlockedは、そのコマンドが復号していないという意味です。既存Proxyの稼働はstatusのProxy欄で別に確認します。
  • ロックで実行中の作業は止まります。先に成果を保存してください。
  • 通常のProxy停止・ホスト再起動でも、プロセスメモリの鍵は失われます。
  • OSキーリングのロックだけでは、起動済みProxyの鍵は消えません。profile lockで別に停止します。このコマンドはOSキーリング自体をロックしません。
  • 暗号化に未対応の古いProxyイメージは更新が必要です。実行中ワーカーを排出してから再作成します。

docs.location: guides/encrypted-credentials/#既存の平文を移行する
docs.title: 既存の平文を移行する
docs.text:
1. 成果を保存して対象ワーカーを停止。
  2. 認証Proxyを停止。
  3. 明示的に移行。
oaiso auth profile encrypt work
  • 暗号化保存・再読込の検証後に平文のwork.jsonを削除。
  • 接続世代を更新するため、旧ワーカーの再認可は拒否します。新しく起動してください。
  • 移行途中で両ファイルが残ると、通常利用を拒否します。同じコマンドとパスフレーズで内容を照合して移行を完了。
  • 内容が異なる場合は自動削除しません。
  • 過去のbackupや削除済みディスクブロックの安全な消去までは保証しません。

docs.location: guides/encrypted-credentials/#旧暗号化形式からageへ移行する
docs.title: 旧暗号化形式からageへ移行する
docs.text:
oaiso auth profile show work
oaiso auth profile lock work
oaiso auth profile migrate-age work
oaiso init --agent codex
  • showのFormat: legacy-v1が対象。新しい形式はFormat: age。
  • 作業を保存してからlock。旧Proxyを停止・削除し、旧パスフレーズまたはキーリングで移行します。
  • age保存・再読込の検証後に切り替え、接続世代を更新。旧ワーカーは新しく作成してください。
  • work.vault.v1-backupを0600の暗号文で残します。通常利用で自動的に読み込みません。
  • 中断時は同じコマンドで再試行できます。異なる内容のbackupを上書きしません。
  • 移行済みの再実行は内容を検証し、世代を再度更新しません。
  • キーリング方式では、backupの復旧用に旧キーリング項目も残します。確認後に管理者が整理してください。
  • 旧形式の新規Proxy起動と更新保存は拒否します。平文やホスト認証へ切り替えません。
  • ホストのsetup --rollbackはプロファイル形式を戻しません。旧版への復旧では再認証を基本とし、旧ワーカーを再開しないでください。

docs.location: guides/encrypted-credentials/#パスフレーズを変更する
docs.title: パスフレーズを変更する
docs.text:
oaiso auth profile lock work
oaiso auth profile passwd work
  • 旧パスフレーズで解錠後、新しいパスフレーズを2回入力。
  • 対象の停止済みProxyを削除してから、同じage秘密identityと認証鍵を新しいパスフレーズで保護し直します。
  • 起動中ワーカー・Proxyがあれば変更を拒否。OSキーリング方式のパスフレーズ変更には使えません。
  • 新しいパスフレーズでoaiso initを実行してProxyを起動します。

docs.title: 非対話で解錠する
docs.text:
oaiso --passphrase-fd 3 init --agent codex 3< /private/runtime/passphrase-input
  • 例は専用FDの接続方法です。入力元は利用者が管理する秘密入力・一時pipe等を使い、パスフレーズをプロジェクトや暗号文の隣へ保存しないでください。
  • FDは3以上、最大4096バイト。末尾の改行1個を除去。APIキーのstdinとは別にします。
  • 秘密を引数・環境変数に入れる入力方法は提供しません。
  • passwdの非対話変更は、旧入力に--passphrase-fd、新入力に--new-passphrase-fdを別々に指定。

docs.location: guides/encrypted-credentials/#保存形式と保護の範囲
docs.title: 保存形式と保護の範囲
docs.text:
項目 仕様 保存先 ~/.config/codex-dock/profiles/NAME/NAME.vault、0700ディレクトリ・0600ファイル ファイル構成 age形式の暗号文・保護済み鍵ファイルを含むJSON manifest。.vault全体をageコマンドへ直接は渡せない 暗号 age v1.3.2のX25519 recipient。公開鍵だけで差し替えられないようHMAC-SHA256でも検証 鍵束の保護 ageのscrypt、logN=17（約128 MiB）。起動時の解錠だけで実行 OSキーリング age秘密identityと認証鍵の鍵束を、既存Secret Serviceへ保存 秘密の所在 ホストの解錠中プロセスと認証Proxyのメモリ。作業VMには仮トークンのみ 主な保護対象 停止中の保存ファイル・ディスク・backupの読取り 保護できないもの ホストroot・同じUIDのプロセス読取り、稼働メモリ・swap・外側VM snapshot
  • WSLではLinux側の私有領域を使用。DrvFS・NFS・FUSE等の未検証filesystemを拒否します。Kata起動には別途KVM条件が必要です。
  • パスフレーズ・キーリングの鍵を失うと復号できません。新しいプロファイルで再認証してください。
  • 鍵を含むVM snapshotの巻戻しは、ローカルだけで完全には検知できません。
  • 形式・保存契約の詳細、動作確認と未確認事項。

docs.title: キーリングで認証情報の鍵を管理する
docs.text:
日本語 | English

  • 開発版の機能です。公開済みv0.0.2には含まれません。
  • 新規のoaiso loginはキーリング保存が既定です。既存プロファイルの方式は変更しません。
  • APIキー・OAuthトークンはageで暗号化した.vaultへ保存。キーリングにはage秘密鍵と改ざん検証用の鍵を保存します。
  • 作業VMにはキーリング・D-Busソケット・実資格情報を渡しません。

docs.title: 環境に合う起動方法
docs.text:
環境 操作 デスクトップのキーリングが利用可能 通常のoaiso loginを実行。解錠済みなら追加入力不要 SSH・WSL・GUIなしのVM oaiso auth keyring sessionで専用セッションを開く キーリングを使用しない login --encryptで製品用パスフレーズ方式を選ぶ 明示的に平文保存する login --plaintext。0700ディレクトリ・0600ファイル
  • GUI・TPM・USBキーは不要です。
  • キーリングが利用不能なら保存を拒否し、別方式へ自動変更しません。提供元へのログインを始める前に保存・取得・削除を確認します。

docs.title: 1. 依存を準備する
docs.text:
• 開発版のoaiso setupは、不足するD-Bus・GNOME Keyring・secret-toolを導入します。
  • オフライン配置では事前に同じパッケージが必要です。
  • 手動導入するUbuntu環境の例：
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install --no-install-recommends dbus-daemon gnome-keyring libsecret-tools
ツール 役割・公式資料 D-Bus 利用者のプロセス間通信。公式手順 GNOME Keyring 鍵の保管・解錠。公式プロジェクト・daemonの操作 secret-tool Secret Serviceへの保存・取得・削除。公式実装
  • GNOMEのデスクトップ全体は不要です。配布パッケージの依存としてGUI関連ライブラリが入る場合はあります。

docs.location: guides/keyring/#2-デスクトップで利用する
docs.title: 2. デスクトップで利用する
docs.text:
oaiso auth keyring check
oaiso login --agent codex --method subscription --profile work
oaiso init --agent codex

Keyring: ready (store/read/delete verified; no provider request).
  • checkはランダムな試験項目だけを保存・再取得・削除します。既存の秘密は表示しません。
  • DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESSが未設定でも、0700・本人所有の利用者runtimeディレクトリにあるbusソケットを探索します。
  • OS側でPAM連携されていれば、ログインパスワードによってキーリングも解錠されます。OaisoがOSパスワードを取得する処理はありません。
  • PAM設定は自動変更しません。SSH公開鍵認証など、OSパスワードを入力しないログインでは別途キーリングの解錠が必要です。PAMの公式説明。

docs.title: 3. GUIなしで利用する
docs.text:
oaiso auth keyring session
  1. 初回は専用パスフレーズを非表示で2回入力。次回は1回。
  2. D-BusとGNOME Keyringを起動し、専用のキーリングを解錠。
  3. 開いたシェルで通常のコマンドを実行。
oaiso auth keyring check
oaiso login --agent claude --method api-key --profile claude-work
oaiso init --agent claude
oaiso claude
exit
  • セッション用のパスフレーズは12〜4096バイト。OSのログインパスワードとは独立です。
  • GNOME Keyringの保存先は~/.config/codex-dock/keyring/keyrings/。デスクトップのキーリングとは分離します。
  • セッション内の複数CLIが、同じ解錠済みサービスを利用します。
  • シェル終了時に専用キーリングとD-Busを終了。暗号化した保管ファイルは保持します。
  • 同じ保管先の専用セッションを同時に2つ開くことは拒否します。
  • シェルを終了しても、起動済み認証Proxyはメモリの鍵を保持します。Proxyもロックする場合は、終了前にoaiso auth profile lock NAMEを実行してください。
  • 次回、専用キーリングに保管したプロファイルを解錠する場合も、keyring session内で操作します。

コマンド1つだけを実行する場合：

oaiso auth keyring session -- oaiso auth keyring check
  • 非対話入力はグローバルの--passphrase-fdで専用FDを指定できます。パスフレーズを引数・環境変数・平文ファイルへ保存しないでください。

docs.title: 既存プロファイル
docs.text:
• 既存の0600平文・パスフレーズ形式はそのまま利用できます。
  • 保存方式を切り替える場合は、キーリングが利用可能な環境で別名の新しいプロファイルへログインしてください。
  • キーリング間の自動コピーや、既存パスフレーズ形式の自動変換は行いません。
  • ageの形式・ロック操作、検証結果と未確認事項。

docs.title: 一般通信を許可する
docs.text:
日本語 | English

docs.location: guides/networking/#1-ホスト側の許可先を設定
docs.title: 1. ホスト側の許可先を設定
docs.text:
• 設定先：~/.config/codex-dock/config.toml。
  • 以下はGitHubとnpmの例。実際に必要な配布先・redirect先も確認して追加。
  • 既存の [proxy] へ統合し、admin_secret_file など他のキーを残す。
[proxy]
forward_default_deny = true
forward_allow_domains = ["github.com", "registry.npmjs.org"]
forward_allow_ports = [80, 443]
指定 意味 github.com その名前とサブドメインを許可 =api.github.com その名前だけに完全一致 ポートだけの許可 宛先の許可にはならない 許可ドメインとCIDRの両方を指定 両方を満たす必要あり。拒否リストは常に優先 private・loopback・metadata宛て CIDR許可でも解除できない
  • GitHubのasset配布など、別ドメインへの移動先は上の例に含まれない。
  • SSH・JVM・独自CA：互換設定も確認。

docs.title: 2. 起動前に確認
docs.text:
oaiso policy check --json
oaiso policy explain registry.npmjs.org:443 --json

2つ目のコマンドの出力例（上の許可設定を使用）

{
  "destination": {"Host": "registry.npmjs.org", "Port": 443},
  "allowed": true,
  "code": "address_not_checked",
  "stage": "destination",
  "addresses_checked": 0,
  "complete": false
}
  • JSONは読みやすく整形。CLIは1行で出力。
  • allowed: true・complete: false：名前とポートの検査を通過。DNSのIP検査は未実施で、実通信の成功を意味しない。
  • policy check：設定が妥当なら終了コード 0 と設定JSONを返す。source は configuration for NEW workers; not a live update。

許可していない宛先も確認

oaiso policy explain example.com:443 --json

{
  "destination": {"Host": "example.com", "Port": 443},
  "allowed": false,
  "code": "domain_not_allowed",
  "stage": "destination",
  "addresses_checked": 0,
  "complete": true
}
  • この例の拒否は正常。explain 自体は正常終了するため、許可・拒否は終了コードではなく allowed / code で判断。

  • 宛先許可が未設定：code: general_egress_disabled。固定AI経路の利用可否とは別。

  • 対象：新規ワーカー向けのホスト設定。稼働中の通信変更ではない。

  • explain：接続しない。上の例は名前・ポートだけを確認。
  • --resolve を追加：DNS応答のIPも確認。実サービスへの疎通試験ではない。
  • TUIで編集する場合：oaiso proxy configure。ノード停止中も利用可。

docs.location: guides/networking/#3-新しいワーカーへ適用
docs.title: 3. 新しいワーカーへ適用
docs.text:
今の状態 操作 初回準備中 設定後、クイックスタートの init へ進む 既存Proxy・ワーカーあり 成果保存 → ワーカー停止・削除 → 対象Proxyを停止・削除 → 新設定で init → 新規ワーカー
  • 設定の保存だけでは既存Proxy・CONNECT・ワーカーへ反映されない。
  • 手順と対象名：Proxy再作成。
  • ワーカー別の --egress-allow-domain とプリセット：ホストの許可を狭める指定。ホスト未許可の宛先は追加できない。

docs.title: 4. 実行後に確認・停止
docs.text:
oaiso policy show --worker WORKER --json
oaiso policy events --worker WORKER --json
  • WORKER：oaiso ps -a に表示された名前へ置換。
  • 拒否履歴：同じegress Proxyを使うワーカー間で共有。実行ごとの独立監査ログではない。
  • すぐに遮断する場合：oaiso policy quarantine --worker WORKER。通信と全ジョブを停止し、そのワーカーの再起動を禁止。
  • 隔離後の成果・保持期限・失敗時の扱い：隔離の仕様。
  • 判定規則の詳細：通信ポリシー。
